title: The AI chat textarea, the support-ticket reply box and four other user-facing inputs have only a placeholder, no accessible name
description: A scan of all 144 Input/Textarea/input/textarea/select elements in app/, components/ and lib/ found these with no id + htmlFor pair, no aria-label and no wrapping <label>: components/ai-chat/chat-widget.tsx:1541 (the AI assistant's message box, mounted on every page via ChatWidget in app/layout.tsx:190); components/contact/support-tickets.tsx:609 (the reply box on a support ticket, available on every tier); components/history/history-notes.tsx:82 (scan notes); components/teams/team-detail-header.tsx:79 (rename a team); app/docs/api/playground/page.tsx:406 (request-body textarea, the sibling of AUDIT-011#docs-07's :514 which cited only the param inputs); components/admin/features/support-inbox.tsx:344 (staff reply). Each has a `placeholder` only, and a placeholder is not an accessible name: it is not exposed as the field's name by the accname algorithm when it is the sole source in several screen-reader/browser pairings, and it disappears the moment the user types. This is the same defect AUDIT-011#docs-07 filed against the playground, present on the general product surface rather than in docs. app/legal/accessibility/page.tsx:88-91 publishes "Form Labels: All form inputs have associated labels for clarity."
impact: A screen-reader user who tabs into the AI support widget hears "edit, blank" with no indication of what the field is for, and the same on a support-ticket reply. Voice-control users cannot say "click <field name>" because there is no name to speak. The published claim is false on the product's own support channel.
recommendation: Add `aria-label` where a visible label would crowd the layout (chat-widget.tsx:1541 `aria-label="Message ${BOT_NAME}"`, support-tickets.tsx:609 and support-inbox.tsx:344 `aria-label="Reply"`, team-detail-header.tsx:79 `aria-label="Team name"`), and give history-notes.tsx:82 a real `useId()`-backed `<label htmlFor>` since it already has a visible "Notes" heading to reuse.

title: The OpenAPI spec omits ten HTTP methods that exist on paths it already documents
description: Mechanically diffing the 20 path items in lib/api/openapi-spec.ts:56-677 against the exported handlers in the matching route.ts files: /history documents GET but the route also exports DELETE (app/api/v3/history/route.ts:153); /history/{id} documents GET but the route also exports PATCH (:194) and DELETE (:392); /scan/remediation documents POST but the route also exports GET (:147) and DELETE (:116); /schedules documents GET+POST but the route also exports PATCH (:223) and DELETE (:322); /teams documents GET+POST but the route also exports PATCH (:129) and DELETE (:176). Ten real operations, on paths the spec already lists, are missing. app/docs/triage/page.tsx:383-394 and app/docs/teams/page.tsx:447-509 document most of them in prose, so the spec is the outlier, not the routes.
impact: The playground renders only what the spec lists (app/docs/api/playground/page.tsx:61-104), so a user can create a schedule or a team from it but cannot rename, pause or delete one, and cannot clear or annotate history. Anyone generating a client SDK from the spec gets a write-only API for those resources.
recommendation: Add the ten missing operations to lib/api/openapi-spec.ts (delete on /history and /history/{id}, patch on /history/{id}, get+delete on /scan/remediation with its ?url= and ?findingId= query params, patch+delete on /schedules and /teams), and extend tests/lib/api/openapi-spec.test.ts with a check that every documented path's method set matches the route file's exports.

title: The compiled AI knowledge truncates 20 of 52 docs callouts mid-sentence at 300 characters and leaks 64 raw JSX `{" "}` tokens and 19 undecoded HTML entities
description: scripts/compile-docs-knowledge.mjs:274 and :284 both apply `stripJsx(...).slice(0, 300)` to every DocsCallout body. Measured across app/docs/*/page.tsx, 52 callouts are extracted and 20 exceed 300 stripped characters, so they land in lib/ai/docs-knowledge.md cut mid-word: for example the API page's Scopes callout ends at "returns 403 naming" (docs-knowledge.md:997) and the CI/CD callout ends at "before ch" (:1009). The offending pages are app/docs/api (2), config (2), github (2), rate-limits (2), scheduled-scans (2), self-hosting (4), sharing (2), account-security, developers, teams and triage. stripJsx (:82-110) also never strips the JSX whitespace literal `{" "}` (64 occurrences survive into the output) and never decodes `'`, `{` or `}` (19 occurrences), so those consume part of the same 300-char budget.
impact: lib/ai/docs-knowledge.md is what the in-product AI assistant answers from. Twenty of the most important "be careful about this" notes reach it as unfinished sentences, so the assistant either invents the missing half or drops the caveat. The Scopes callout in particular loses the sentence that tells the user a 403 names the missing scope.
recommendation: Raise the cap in scripts/compile-docs-knowledge.mjs:274/284 to at least 1200 characters (the longest real callout is 522), or truncate on a sentence boundary; and add `.replace(/\{\s*"\s*"\s*\}/g, " ")` plus `'`/`&#\d+;` decoding to stripJsx before the existing entity replacements.

title: Half of .github/labeler.yml uses an invented schema the labeler action silently ignores, so the step named "Apply size label" has never applied a size label
description: actions/labeler takes the label name as the top-level key and accepts only `changed-files`, `base-branch`, `head-branch`, `any` and `all` as matcher keys. .github/labeler.yml gets this right for four blocks (`ci` line 24, `config` line 29, `security` line 35, `docs` line 39) and wrong for the other two. The `size` block (lines 3-16) has a top-level key `size` whose entries are `{label: "size/xs", files: [...]}`, and the `dependencies` block (lines 18-21) uses `{label: "dependencies", from-branch: [...]}`. `label`, `files` and `from-branch` are not matcher keys. I confirmed against the action's source (src/api/get-label-configs.ts): an unrecognised key is not an error, it hits `core.info(\`An unknown config option was under ${label}: ${key}\`)` and produces no matcher, so the labels `size`, `size/xs`, `size/s`, `size/m`, `size/l` and the branch-based `dependencies` rule are never applied. The step at .github/workflows/label.yml:16 is literally named "Apply size label". Separately, label.yml:7-8 declares `permissions: pull-requests: write` only; declaring any permission sets every unlisted scope to `none`, including `contents`, while the action's documented usage requires `contents: read` to read the configuration file from the repository.
impact: PR triage silently does not work. Maintainers see no size labels, and the `dependencies` label the stale.yml exemption logic and the auto-merge ignore flow both reason about is never applied from the branch name (dependabot supplies it from .github/dependabot.yml:12-14 instead, which masks the breakage). Nothing in the log makes this visible except an `info`-level line nobody reads.
recommendation: Rewrite the `size` and `dependencies` blocks in .github/labeler.yml to the real schema: one top-level key per label (`size/xs:`, `size/s:`, ...) with `- changed-files: - any-glob-to-any-file: [...]`, and `dependencies: - head-branch: ["^dependabot/"]`. Note that labeler matches on paths, not diff size, so if a real size label is wanted use a line-count action instead. Add `contents: read` to the permissions block in .github/workflows/label.yml:7.

title: The GitHub Action gate stops at severity counts and never uploads the SARIF the API already produces, so findings never reach the Security tab that ZAP, Nuclei and Snyk actions all populate
description: The composite action at .github/actions/scan-gate/action.yml is complete and correct: it starts a scan, polls GET /scan/status, and at :152 to :176 reads only summary.critical/high/medium/low/total, writes a step summary table, and exits 1 on threshold breach. It never fetches SARIF. A full SARIF 2.1.0 generator already exists at lib/reports/sarif-report.ts:1 and is exposed as GET /api/v3/history/[id]/report?format=sarif (app/api/v3/history/[id]/report/route.ts:174), and app/docs/reports/page.tsx:310 to :319 already publishes the exact two-step recipe (curl the SARIF, then github/codeql-action/upload-sarif@v3) as something the user must hand-assemble. The action already emits scan-id as an output (.github/actions/scan-gate/action.yml:45), so the two halves are one curl apart. Separately, the action lives at .github/actions/scan-gate/ inside the app repo, which is not a GitHub Marketplace-publishable location: Marketplace requires action.yml at the root of its own repository plus a tagged release. ZAP ships official Marketplace actions, Nuclei ships one, and Snyk and Burp both list Actions integrations (audits/AUDIT-014/research-competitors.md, ZAP and Nuclei sections).
impact: A developer wiring VulnRadar into CI gets a red X and a markdown table, while the equivalent ZAP or Nuclei action gets them annotated Code Scanning alerts inline on the pull-request diff, with dismissal and tracking handled by GitHub. That is the difference between a gate people keep and a gate people delete after the second false alarm. And because the action is not on the Marketplace, the highest-intent discovery channel for this product (a developer searching the Actions marketplace for "security scan") returns nothing.
recommendation: Two changes, both small. First, in .github/actions/scan-gate/action.yml add an optional `sarif-file` input (default `vulnradar.sarif`); after the poll loop succeeds, curl `$VR_API_BASE/history/$scan_id/report?format=sarif` to that path and add a `sarif-file` output, then document the follow-on `github/codeql-action/upload-sarif` step in app/docs/api/page.tsx:1299's snippet so the published example is the complete one. Second, mirror the action into a dedicated `VulnRadar/scan-gate-action` repo with action.yml at the root and a v1 tag, publish it to the Marketplace, and change the `uses:` in app/docs/api/page.tsx:1299 from the current `${APP_REPO}/.github/actions/scan-gate@main` (an unpinned branch reference) to `VulnRadar/scan-gate-action@v1`.

title: There is no overall A+ to F grade, so the badge and public host report speak safe/caution/unsafe and cannot occupy the vocabulary SecurityHeaders.com just vacated
category: list (a) gap rank 3: the grading vocabulary and the badge flywheel
description: Four of the free peers grade a whole site on one A+ to F scale: MDN HTTP Observatory (A+ down to F, ten header tests), SecurityHeaders.com (A+ to F on response headers), Qualys SSL Labs (A+ to F plus T and M), and ImmuniWeb (grade-gated PDF certificate plus installable badge). VulnRadar has the scoring machinery but not the vocabulary. lib/scanner/ssl-grade.ts:1 already computes a real SSL-Labs-style A+/A/B/C/D/F letter, but only for the TLS handshake. The whole-scan verdict is a three-state safety rating (lib/scanner/safety-rating.ts:19, "safe" | "caution" | "unsafe") plus a 0-10 danger score (:306), and the embeddable badge renders exactly that three-state label (app/api/v3/badge/[token]/route.ts:99 to :115). Confirmed live this session: Snyk shut down the securityheaders.com API in April 2026 (announced January 2026), leaving only the free web scanner; the replacements ranking for "securityheaders alternative" are unknown micro-vendors (WebAudit, Guardr, detectzestack, myssl.info, sitesecurityscore). SSL Labs v4 requires an organizational email and forbids commercial use by default, and MDN Observatory dropped TLS entirely in October 2024. The auto-updating badge infrastructure already exists and is idempotent per (user, url) so an embed never breaks (app/api/v3/badge/site/route.ts:8).
impact: A README badge that says "caution" is a liability the owner removes; a badge that says "A" is a trophy the owner keeps and that links back. ImmuniWeb built 380M+ scans on exactly that mechanic and gates the certificate on the grade so people work to earn it. VulnRadar has the badge, the public host page, the API, and TLS plus DNS plus header coverage that the vacated SecurityHeaders niche wants, and cannot be compared against the incumbent because it does not speak the incumbent's scale.
recommendation: Add `getSiteGrade(findings): "A+"|"A"|"B"|"C"|"D"|"F"` to lib/scanner/safety-rating.ts, derived from the existing danger score and severity weights so it stays deterministic and needs no new detection work, and document the exact deduction table on a public page the way lib/scanner/ssl-grade.ts:20 already documents its own. Render the grade as the primary label in app/api/v3/badge/[token]/route.ts:99 (keep safe/caution/unsafe as the badge's secondary colour semantics), lead with it on app/host/[hostname]/page.tsx, and gate the shareable badge on B or better, matching ImmuniWeb. Then publish a keyless or free-key-tier grading endpoint documented in app/docs/api as the drop-in for the dead securityheaders.com API, using the existing demo-scan rate-limit shape (app/api/v3/demo-scan/route.ts:97) rather than the account-gated /api/v3/scan.

title: Authenticated scanning ships form, header and cookie login but no recorded multi-step sequence, no TOTP, no SSO/OIDC login, and no re-authentication when the target drops the session mid-scan
category: list (a) gap rank 5: authenticated scanning, narrowed against the code
description: The research called authenticated scanning the single biggest gap and flagged it for verification. Verified in code, the gap is much narrower than that. lib/scanner/auth/types.ts:13 declares `ScanAuthType = "form" | "header" | "cookie"`, all three are implemented (lib/scanner/auth/login.ts, lib/scanner/auth/browser-login.ts), and the form path is better than a naive implementation: it opens a real headless browser session to render a client-side login form before parsing it (lib/scanner/auth/browser-login.ts:1 to :27). POST /api/v3/scan/authenticated exists (app/api/v3/scan/authenticated/route.ts:56), the session is origin-bound with a logout guard (lib/scanner/auth/scan-session.ts:104 to :113), and the crawl engine reports the auth state back. What is genuinely absent: (1) multi-step or recorded login sequences, a browser-recorder capture of the click path (Detectify ships a Chrome recorder, Astra uses Chrome DevTools Recorder, Pentest-Tools and Acunetix both ship a login sequence recorder, Snyk supports recorded sequences); (2) TOTP or OTP second factor, which Astra and Snyk both handle and Acunetix explicitly claims for MFA and CAPTCHA; (3) SSO or OpenID Connect login flows, which only Snyk supports; (4) automatic re-authentication when the session dies mid-scan. On (4), lib/scanner/auth/scan-session.ts:86 `markLost()` records the loss and :116 to :154 detects all three loss signals (cleared session cookie, 401/403, redirect back to the login path), but nothing ever calls establishScanSession again: a grep for re-auth, reauth, relogin across lib/scanner/ and app/api/v3/scan/ returns zero hits. Snyk is the only one of the eight with automatic re-auth mid-scan.
impact: For this product's users (developers scanning their own staging app behind a login) the practical bite is ordered opposite to the market's marketing. Item (4) costs users today: a long crawl of a session-expiring app silently degrades to an anonymous scan partway through and reports status "lost", so the user pays a scan against their daily quota and gets a partial result they must re-run by hand. Items (1) to (3) cost the product a specific class of prospect (SPAs with a multi-screen login, any team with 2FA enforced on staging) but each is expensive to build and none is a same-day fix.
recommendation: Build (4) first, alone: it is the smallest change and the only one costing users today. In lib/scanner/execute-crawl-scan.ts, when the binding reports `lost`, call `establishScanSession` once more with the same EphemeralAuthInput held in memory for that request, cap re-auth at two attempts per scan, and record the count in ScanAuthReport (lib/scanner/auth/types.ts:85) so the result says "re-authenticated once" rather than "lost". Then add TOTP as (2): it is a `totpSecret` field on EphemeralFormAuth (lib/scanner/auth/types.ts:21), an otpauth-style code generator, and one extra form submit in lib/scanner/auth/browser-login.ts, and it unlocks every target with authenticator-app 2FA. Defer (1) recorded sequences and (3) SSO: a recorder needs a browser extension capture format, a step-replay engine on top of the BrowserBase CDP path, and stored (not ephemeral) sequence definitions, which contradicts the deliberate never-persisted credential model documented at lib/scanner/auth/types.ts:1 to :10. That model is itself an advantage worth keeping; see comp-10.

title: Ticketing stops at one one-way GitHub issue holding up to 50 findings, with no per-finding issue, no close-the-loop retest, and no Jira or Linear
category: list (a) gap rank 8: issue tracker integration
description: Jira is universal across all eight commercial vendors, Slack near-universal, and the real differentiator is two-way sync: Detectify's Jira integration updates the finding when the ticket is resolved, and Probely/Snyk goes further, marking the Jira issue Done automatically triggers a retest of that finding. Linear appears only at Intruder (audits/AUDIT-014/research-competitors-commercial.md, "Table stakes" item 2). VulnRadar's entire ticketing surface is POST /api/v3/scan/github-issue (app/api/v3/scan/github-issue/route.ts:11), which files one issue per scan into one repo, listing at most 50 findings in the body (`MAX_FINDINGS_LISTED = 50`, :26). It is one-way and one-shot: nothing reads the issue's state back, nothing closes it when a rescan shows the finding gone, and there is no per-finding issue so no finding has its own trackable ticket. Notification delivery is limited to Discord, Slack and generic webhooks (lib/webhooks/detect-type.ts:7 to :14) plus email; there is no Jira, Linear, ServiceNow or Teams destination anywhere in lib/.
impact: For the developer this product targets, a single 50-item issue is a dump, not a workflow: it cannot be assigned, prioritised, or closed piecemeal, and once one finding is fixed the issue is stale but still open. For the small security team, the absence of any close-the-loop mechanism means the remediation state lives only inside VulnRadar (lib/scanner/remediation-store.ts) and inside the tracker separately, and the two drift.
recommendation: Do not start with Jira. The GitHub connection already exists, is already authorised for issue writes (lib/github/github-connections.ts), and the finding IDs are already stable across runs (lib/scanner/_helpers.ts generateId, `<checkId>--<urlHash>`), which is exactly what a close-the-loop integration needs and what Jira would still need built. Extend app/api/v3/scan/github-issue/route.ts with a per-finding mode: one issue per finding, titled with the check id, labelled by severity, and stamped with the stable finding id in the body. Then in lib/scanner/regression-alert.ts, which already diffs a completed scan against the previous scan of the same URL by that same id, close any tracked issue whose finding is absent from the new scan and post a one-line comment saying which scan proved it fixed. That is the Probely/Snyk retest loop, built on machinery that already exists. Add Jira only if a paying user asks for it by name.

title: Authenticated scanning here never stores a credential and the product ships zero telemetry, a privacy posture no SaaS peer can match, and it is stated nowhere outside a source-file comment
description: lib/scanner/auth/types.ts:1 to :10 documents a deliberate design: "There is no stored credential anywhere in this codebase: a caller supplies login material directly in a single scan request, it lives in memory for the length of that one request, and it is never written to a table, a log line, an audit record, or the persisted scan result." The route enforces it (app/api/v3/scan/authenticated/route.ts:56 to :68: logAction records only the non-secret outcome), and the session object reports counts rather than contents (lib/scanner/auth/scan-session.ts:157 to :172). Every one of the eight commercial vendors stores your target credentials in their SaaS by construction, because all of them offer saved recorded login sequences. Separately, components/landing/landing-open-source.tsx:6 to :13 already lists "Telemetry: None" and "Third-party trackers: None" as bare facts in a definition list. The privacy argument is never made anywhere: neither claim appears in any /alternatives comparison row (lib/seo/alternatives.ts:44 has no privacy or data-handling row), in any landing FAQ answer (app/landing/page.tsx), or on the pricing page.
impact: "Do I have to give a third-party SaaS a working login to my staging environment" is the objection that kills authenticated-scanning trials, and it is the one objection this product has an unusually good answer to. Burying that answer in a TypeScript file comment means it never reaches the person deciding.
recommendation: Add a `privacy` row to the shared VR object in lib/seo/alternatives.ts:44: "Login material is sent in one request and held in memory for that request only. Never stored, logged, or written to a scan result." and give each competitor an accurate neutral `them` ("Saved login sequences, stored vendor-side"). Add it to the authenticated-scanning UI as a one-line reassurance above the credential fields, and to app/docs/ wherever authenticated scanning is documented. Pair it with the two existing facts from components/landing/landing-open-source.tsx:10 to :11 into a short "What we never keep" block on the landing page, which is a genuinely different section shape from the icon grids CLAUDE.md's design rules ban.

title: Active probing is nine reflection-and-error-based probes with no out-of-band channel, so blind injection, stored XSS and second-order flaws are structurally undetectable and the marketing should say so
category: list (a) gap rank 11: depth of active testing
description: The research called active injection testing the defining line and ranked it gap number one. Verified in code, VulnRadar is further along than that implies but structurally capped. lib/scanner/active-probe-catalog.ts:46 to :101 defines nine opt-in probes, gated behind verified domain ownership (:117): reflected XSS canary, error-based SQLi, SSTI, OS command injection, confirmed open redirect, GraphQL introspection, active CORS reflection, dangerous HTTP methods, and X-Forwarded-Host injection, implemented in lib/scanner/active-probes/ (five modules, roughly 700 lines). Every one of them decides from the immediate response body or status. There is no out-of-band interaction server anywhere in the repo (grep for oast, collaborator, interactsh across lib/scanner/ returns only unrelated matches in port-scan.ts and two checks-data JSON files), which means blind and time-based SQLi, blind SSRF, blind XXE, out-of-band command injection and Log4Shell-class flaws cannot be confirmed by construction. There is also no second request-cycle verification, so stored XSS is out of reach. By contrast ZAP and Wapiti send full active-scan payloads across 30+ module families including XXE, path traversal, file upload and CSRF, Nuclei adds fuzzing with -dast, Burp ships OAST via Collaborator, Pentest-Tools ships actual auto-exploiters, and Invicti claims runtime proof-based verification at 99.98%.
impact: Two-sided. Against ZAP and Wapiti, VulnRadar genuinely finds less, and a security engineer who assumes "active probing" means ZAP-equivalent coverage will conclude the scanner missed things it never claimed to look for. Against the free graders (Observatory, SecurityHeaders, SSL Labs), VulnRadar finds far more, which is the comparison that actually matters for its funnel. The cost today is not missed findings so much as an unstated ceiling.
recommendation: Do not build an OAST server. It needs a public wildcard DNS zone plus an always-on HTTP collector, it breaks in every self-hosted deployment (which is the differentiator in comp-01), and it is the single most expensive item on this list. If out-of-band detection is ever wanted, integrate the public interactsh server as an optional, off-by-default setting rather than operating one. What is worth doing now is cheap and honest: state the ceiling. Add one line to the active-probes description surface (lib/scanner/active-probe-catalog.ts:44's rendered panel and app/checks/category/active-probes) saying these probes confirm what the response itself proves and do not attempt blind or time-based detection, and add an /alternatives entry for OWASP ZAP that says plainly that ZAP sends deeper payloads while VulnRadar is the hosted, zero-setup, public-catalog path. Being the tool that documents its own limits is a positioning asset for a scanner whose core pitch is determinism.

title: AGENTS.md lists 12 of the scanner's 18 categories, so an automated contributor is told six live categories do not exist
description: AGENTS.md:140-153 gives the authoritative category list an agent must consult 'Before adding a scanner' and names 12: headers, ssl, tls, content, cookies, configuration, information-disclosure, dns, email, api, code, secrets-extended. The Category union at lib/scanner/types.ts:22-39 has 18, adding vibe-code, client-side, supply-chain, host-validation, reputation and active-probes. lib/config/check-stats.generated.ts:7 records EXACT_CHECK_CATEGORY_COUNT = 18, README.md:12 and :30 say 18, and the browser extension's own list at extension/src/lib/categories.ts has all 18. AGENTS.md is the only surface that disagrees, and it has a matching lib/scanner/checks-data/<category>.json for each of the six it omits.
impact: An automated contributor following AGENTS.md sees no vibe-code, client-side, supply-chain, host-validation, reputation or active-probes category and will either refuse to place a check there or invent a new category rather than using the existing one. active-probes matters most: it is the only opt-in, writes-to-the-target category (lib/scanner/types.ts:41-50 explains why it is excluded from ALL_CATEGORIES) and an agent that does not know it exists cannot honour that contract.
recommendation: Replace the hand-written list in AGENTS.md:140-153 with the 18 names from lib/scanner/types.ts, or better, replace it with an instruction to read the Category union directly so it cannot drift again. Add a line stating that active-probes never runs by default and must be named explicitly.

title: Five product surfaces the README advertises have no documentation page: billing and subscription management, bulk scanning, notifications, admin operations, and what to do when a scan fails or reports nothing
description: DOCS_NAV (components/docs/docs-nav.ts:13-140) has 19 entries across six sections. Cross-checking them against the shipped surface: (1) Billing. app/pricing, app/checkout, app/api/v3/billing/route.ts, app/api/v3/billing/subscription/cancel/route.ts and .../reactivate/route.ts exist, four paid plans are defined in lib/billing/catalog.ts, and three separate credit products have checkout components under components/billing/. No docs page explains plans, upgrading, cancelling, reactivating, credits, or what happens at the end of a trial; grepping app/docs for 'cancel' returns only API and team contexts and 'refund' returns one line on the AI page. (2) Bulk scanning. README.md:34 advertises it, app/api/v3/scan/bulk and components/scanner/dashboard-bulk-result.tsx implement it, and 'bulk scan' appears in app/docs only inside the API reference. (3) Notifications. app/api/v3/notifications exists and is referenced from eight docs pages in passing, with no page of its own. (4) Admin. app/admin plus 267 SETTINGS_REGISTRY entries, the audit log, impersonation, broadcasts, the Backup button and IP rules have no operator page; 'audit log' appears in app/docs only in the API reference and 'activity log' nowhere. (5) Troubleshooting a scan. Nothing anywhere covers a scan that fails, times out, or returns zero findings, which is the single most common support question for a scanner.
impact: Every one of these lands in support instead of self-service, and the project has in-app support tickets (app/docs/triage covers them) so the cost is real. Billing is the sharpest: a paying user who wants to cancel has no documentation and must find the button, which is a chargeback and trust risk on a service with a real subscriber base.
recommendation: Add three pages first, in this order: 'Plans and Billing' under Using VulnRadar (what each plan includes rendered from lib/billing/catalog.ts, how to upgrade, cancel and reactivate, how the three credit types work, what happens when a subscription lapses); 'Troubleshooting Scans' (timeouts, blocked targets, zero-finding results, robots.txt exclusions, what each terminal scan status means); and 'Administration' under Running your own (the /admin tabs, the settings registry, the audit log, backups, IP rules, impersonation). Fold bulk scanning into the scheduled-scans page or give it a section, and give notifications a section on the account-security page rather than a page of its own.

title: The product ships two mutually exclusive corner-radius conventions, so the scan result view and /profile are visibly different products sitting one nav item apart
description: audits/AUDIT-011/design-language.md section C5 records the ladder: rounded-2xl for one flagship block, rounded-xl for content cards, code blocks, tables and the readout, rounded-lg for small cards and chip links, rounded-md for buttons. I counted every rounded-* literal per directory. components/scanner: 83 rounded-md, 4 rounded-lg, 0 rounded-xl. components/history: 21 rounded-md, 3 rounded-lg. components/shares, components/assets, components/host, components/teams and components/billing are the same shape (6, 6, 1, 10 and 36 rounded-md respectively). Against that, components/profile is 72 rounded-lg + 24 rounded-xl + 14 rounded-md, and components/admin is 132 rounded-lg + 19 rounded-xl + 26 rounded-md. These are not buttons: filtering to bordered card containers, the scanner family draws its panels at rounded-md (components/scanner/issue-detail.tsx:608,719,837,862, dashboard.tsx:260,342,417,453, response-headers.tsx:46, dns-records-panel.tsx:207, port-scan-panel.tsx:126, threat-intel-panel.tsx, software-inventory-panel.tsx, results-list.tsx:463), while components/profile and components/admin draw the equivalent panels at rounded-lg or rounded-xl (18 and 9 of them respectively), and components/ui/card.tsx:12 (the shared primitive, used by 42 files) is rounded-lg. The landing page, the documented yardstick, uses rounded-xl for content cards. So the same nav bar leads to a 6px-radius scan report and a 12px-radius billing card.
impact: Radius is one of the two or three cues a person uses to decide whether two screens belong to the same application. A user who scans a site and then opens Profile crosses a visible seam. It also makes every new component a coin flip for the author, which is how the split got to 83 versus 132 in the first place.
recommendation: Adopt the landing ladder as written in design-language.md C5 and move the scanner family up, not the profile family down, because the shared primitive components/ui/card.tsx and 42 of its consumers are already on rounded-lg. Concretely: in components/scanner, change the bordered panel containers (issue-detail.tsx:608,719,837,862; dashboard.tsx:172,260,342,417,453; response-headers.tsx:46; dns-records-panel.tsx:207; port-scan-panel.tsx:126; results-list.tsx:463,598; scan-result-detail.tsx:228; crawl-pages-info.tsx:54; dashboard-error-state.tsx:182; scan-summary.tsx) from rounded-md to rounded-xl, and the same in components/history, components/shares, components/assets, components/host and components/teams. Leave rounded-md on the actual controls (inputs at results-list.tsx:379, buttons at :408,615) where it is correct. Then write the three-rung ladder into CLAUDE.md's spacing section so it is reviewable: rounded-xl = panel, rounded-lg = small card or chip, rounded-md = control, rounded-full = pill, rounded-2xl = one flagship block per page.

title: Seven different page-H1 treatments across 71 pages, and the documented Page H1 scale appears on no signed-in page at all
description: design-language.md B2 records the Page H1 (non-hero) as `text-3xl sm:text-4xl font-semibold tracking-tight mb-5 text-balance`, cited from app/pricing/page.tsx:77. I extracted the className of every <h1> in app/ and components/. Seven distinct treatments ship: (1) the documented one, on app/pricing/page.tsx:77, app/checks/page.tsx:75, app/checks/category/[category]/page.tsx:126, app/alternatives/page.tsx:40, app/alternatives/[competitor]/page.tsx:85, app/tools/page.tsx:56, app/tools/api-scanner/page.tsx:79, app/tools/link-checker/page.tsx:80, all of them public SEO pages; (2) `text-xl sm:text-2xl font-semibold tracking-tight text-foreground` on app/history/page.tsx:576, app/assets/page.tsx:148, app/shares/page.tsx:160, app/repos/page.tsx:360,465 and app/public-scans/page.tsx:118; (3) `text-2xl font-semibold tracking-tight` on app/profile/page.tsx:679, app/admin/page.tsx:1021, app/attack-surface/page.tsx:30, app/legal/page.tsx:57 and app/teams/join/page.tsx:29; (4) `text-2xl sm:text-3xl font-semibold tracking-tight` on app/badge/page.tsx:101, app/changelog/page.tsx:22, app/compare/page.tsx:212, app/contact/page.tsx:56 and app/donate/page.tsx:32; (5) `text-lg font-semibold` with no tracking-tight on app/host/[hostname]/page.tsx:144,161,218 and app/shared/[token]/page.tsx:143,251; (6) `font-bold` variants on app/checkout/credits/page.tsx:52,82,145 and its three sibling checkout pages, app/checkout/success/checkout-success-content.tsx:98 and app/security/page.tsx:48; (7) `text-2xl sm:text-4xl` (skipping the 3xl step) on app/checks/[id]/page.tsx:195. Only the SEO family matches the spec. Every page a paying user actually works in is on one of the other six. text-balance, which design-language.md B3 says goes on every heading, is present only on the SEO family, checks/[id] and two modal titles.
impact: A user moving Dashboard to History to Profile to Admin sees the page title change size three times for no reason, so nothing tells them what a page title is. Two of the seven treatments use font-bold, a weight design-language.md B3 records as appearing nowhere in the reference work.
recommendation: Two tiers, written down, then applied. Tier A (marketing, docs, SEO, legal, pricing): keep the documented `text-3xl sm:text-4xl font-semibold tracking-tight mb-5 text-balance`. Tier B (in-app working pages, where the H1 sits above a dense table and must not eat the fold): standardise on `text-xl sm:text-2xl font-semibold tracking-tight text-balance text-foreground`, which treatment (2) already uses on five pages and which is the largest existing cluster. Change app/profile/page.tsx:679, app/admin/page.tsx:1021, app/attack-surface/page.tsx:30, app/badge/page.tsx:101, app/host/[hostname]/page.tsx:218 and app/shared/[token]/page.tsx:251 to Tier B, and app/security/page.tsx:48, app/legal/page.tsx:57, app/changelog/page.tsx:22, app/contact/page.tsx:56 and app/donate/page.tsx:32 to Tier A. Delete every font-bold in an <h1> (checkout pages are covered separately in dsn-05). Add both strings to CLAUDE.md under a Typography heading next to the existing Button and Spacing conventions, which is the only reason the button geometry stayed consistent and the heading scale did not.

title: The four checkout pages are the least spec-conformant surface in the product and they are the revenue path: container mx-auto, py-8 md:py-12, font-bold headings and md: breakpoints, all four times over
description: app/checkout/credits/page.tsx, app/checkout/github-credits/page.tsx, app/checkout/browser-credits/page.tsx and app/checkout/[productId]/page.tsx (plus components/billing/checkout-skeleton.tsx) fail four of the fourteen tell-tale checks in design-language.md G simultaneously, and they are the only files in app/ that do. Check 2 (container): they are the only five files in the repo using Tailwind's `container` class, at credits:119,142, github-credits:121,140, browser-credits:123,142, [productId]:168,192 and checkout-skeleton:13,24, always as `container max-w-4xl mx-auto px-4`, where the documented default is `max-w-6xl mx-auto px-4 sm:px-6` and the responsive px step is missing. Check 1 (section rhythm): `py-8 md:py-12` at credits:142 and its three siblings, against the documented `py-16 sm:py-20`; md: rather than sm: is used for every breakpoint on these pages while the rest of app/ uses sm:. Check 7 (heading scale): `text-2xl font-bold mb-2` at credits:52,82, `text-2xl md:text-3xl font-bold mb-2` at :145, `text-lg font-bold` at :190 and `text-2xl font-bold` at :226, with the same lines in all three credit pages and [productId]:81,100,120,150,198,257. design-language.md B3 records that font-bold appears nowhere in the reference work. The three credit pages are otherwise near-identical files, which AUDIT-013#dup-06 already filed from the code-duplication angle (roughly 1,900 duplicated lines across the three checkout components and three pages); the design consequence is that a single fix has to be made three or four times and has not been.
impact: This is the screen where a user hands over a card. It is visibly heavier and more cramped than the pricing page they arrived from: a bolder title, half the vertical room, a narrower measure and no sm: padding step, so on a 640px phone the page has 16px gutters where /pricing has 24px. It reads as a different, older product at the exact moment trust matters most, and the same four defects have to be fixed four times because the pages were copied.
recommendation: Fix this together with AUDIT-013#dup-06's collapse rather than separately. When the three credit pages fold into one parameterised CreditCheckout page, give the surviving page: `<main id="main-content" tabIndex={-1} className="w-full max-w-4xl mx-auto px-4 sm:px-6 py-12 sm:py-16">` (max-w-4xl is defensible for a single-task form; drop the `container` class, which does nothing here but add Tailwind's own padding), the Tier A page H1 from dsn-04 (`text-3xl sm:text-4xl font-semibold tracking-tight mb-5 text-balance`), `text-lg font-semibold` for the tier price at credits:190, and `text-2xl font-semibold tabular-nums` for the Total today figure at :226. Change every md: breakpoint on these pages to sm: to match the rest of app/. Apply the same to app/checkout/[productId]/page.tsx and components/billing/checkout-skeleton.tsx so the skeleton and the loaded page still line up.

title: Six implementations of one inline stat strip, at three different value type sizes and two container geometries, and two byte-identical copies of the STAT_ICON_TONES table
description: Extends AUDIT-013#dup-12, which caught the Cell duplication between components/assets/assets-stats.tsx:9 and components/shares/shares-stats.tsx:17 and the three identical stats skeletons, from the code angle. It missed four more copies and did not record the visual result. The full set: components/history/history-stats.tsx:18 defines a third byte-identical Cell; components/scanner/dashboard.tsx:94 defines StatCell (the same markup with items-start instead of items-center and no textTone); components/scanner/scan-summary.tsx:75 defines Stat (same again at StatIcon size="sm" with a text-sm value and flex-1 basis-24 instead of a grid); components/admin/shared/stat-card.tsx:52 defines StatBar, a sixth. The value type size differs three ways for the same element: text-2xl in history-stats/assets-stats/shares-stats/dashboard.tsx:108, text-sm in scan-summary.tsx:88, text-lg in stat-card.tsx:82. The container differs two ways: `grid grid-cols-2 sm:grid-cols-4 gap-px bg-border overflow-hidden rounded-md border border-border` in the four app-side copies versus `flex flex-wrap rounded-lg border border-border/50 bg-border/50 gap-px overflow-hidden` at stat-card.tsx:62. On top of that, the STAT_ICON_TONES lookup is duplicated verbatim, nine keys and all their class strings, at components/shared/stat-icon.tsx:11-24 and components/admin/shared/stat-card.tsx:11-24; stat-icon.tsx's own docblock at :4-10 says it exists to stop each file inventing its own colours and then names stat-card.tsx as the pattern it is copying rather than importing from it.
impact: This is the mechanism by which one product stops looking like one product, applied to the element a user meets first on five different pages. The counts row on /dashboard, /history, /assets and /shares is 24px tall type in a 6px-radius box; the same row on /admin is 18px type in an 8px-radius box with a half-opacity border; the same row inside a scan summary is 14px type in a flex strip. Nothing distinguishes them semantically, so a reader learns the pattern four times. Two copies of the tone table mean the next colour added lands in one of them.
recommendation: Promote a single components/shared/stat-strip.tsx exporting `StatStrip({ items, size })` and reusing the existing StatIcon, with size="md" giving today's `text-2xl font-semibold leading-none tabular-nums tracking-tight` value and size="sm" giving `text-sm`, and one container: `flex flex-wrap gap-px overflow-hidden rounded-xl border border-border bg-border` (rounded-xl per dsn-03). Delete Cell from components/history/history-stats.tsx:18, components/assets/assets-stats.tsx:9 and components/shares/shares-stats.tsx:17, StatCell from components/scanner/dashboard.tsx:94, Stat from components/scanner/scan-summary.tsx:75, and rewrite components/admin/shared/stat-card.tsx's StatBar as a thin wrapper that adds only the onClick/aria-pressed filtering behaviour its docblock at :46-51 describes. Delete the STAT_ICON_TONES block at components/admin/shared/stat-card.tsx:11-26 and import StatTone and the tones from components/shared/stat-icon.tsx. Collapse the three stats skeletons AUDIT-013#dup-12 lists into one StatStripSkeleton beside it so the loading state cannot drift from the loaded state again.

title: Five empty-state grammars, four of which are byte-identical wrappers around the same markup with a different icon and sentence
description: Five distinct empty-state treatments ship. (1) The app family, `flex flex-col items-center gap-3 rounded-md border border-dashed border-border bg-card/50 px-4 py-14 text-center` with a 6x6 icon at text-muted-foreground/60, a text-sm font-semibold title, a max-w-xs text-xs body and an optional sm Button: components/history/history-empty-state.tsx:25 and :48, components/assets/assets-empty-state.tsx:20 and :41, components/shares/shares-empty-state.tsx:7, components/public-scans/public-scans-empty-state.tsx:5, components/teams/teams-list.tsx:56 and :72, components/scanner/results-list.tsx:598, components/scanner/dashboard-results.tsx:269 and components/scanner/scan-result-detail.tsx:228. The four standalone files are the same JSX with only the icon and copy swapped, and each is its own module. (2) The admin family, components/admin/shared/data-table.tsx:19-45 EmptyState: no dashed border and no card at all, a 12x12 rounded-full bg-muted/50 circle holding a 6x6 icon at text-muted-foreground/50, py-16 px-4, text-sm font-medium title, text-xs max-w-sm body. Used by roughly 14 admin panels plus app/admin/page.tsx:1301,1502. (3) components/badge/badge-empty-state.tsx:8, `rounded-xl border border-dashed border-border bg-card/30 py-14 px-6`. (4) components/repos/repo-detail.tsx:251, `rounded-lg border border-dashed border-border px-4 py-10` with no background at all. (5) components/profile/tabs/developer/api-keys-section.tsx:250, `rounded-xl border border-dashed border-border bg-muted/20 p-5 sm:p-6` left-aligned. Radius spans md, lg and xl; the surface spans bg-card/50, bg-card/30, bg-muted/20 and nothing; the icon is bare in one family and in a circle in the other.
impact: Empty states are the first thing a new account sees on five pages in a row (/history, /assets, /shares, /teams, the results list) and they are the first thing an admin sees in fourteen panels. Two unrelated grammars for the same moment make the admin panel read as a bolted-on second application, which is exactly how it is built. Four separate one-file modules means a copy change or an a11y fix has to be made four times.
recommendation: Add components/shared/empty-state.tsx exporting `EmptyState({ icon, title, description, action, variant })` with the app family's geometry as the default (`flex flex-col items-center gap-3 rounded-xl border border-dashed border-border bg-card/50 px-4 py-14 text-center`, rounded-xl per dsn-03) and variant="inline" dropping the border and background for use inside a card that already has one, which is what the admin EmptyState is really doing. Delete components/history/history-empty-state.tsx, components/assets/assets-empty-state.tsx, components/shares/shares-empty-state.tsx and components/public-scans/public-scans-empty-state.tsx and call the shared component from the four pages with their icon and copy inline; delete the inline copies at components/teams/teams-list.tsx:56,72, components/scanner/results-list.tsx:598, dashboard-results.tsx:269 and scan-result-detail.tsx:228; re-export the shared component from components/admin/shared/data-table.tsx as EmptyState with variant="inline" so the fourteen admin call sites need no edit, and delete its body at :19-45. Fold components/badge/badge-empty-state.tsx and components/repos/repo-detail.tsx:251 in too.

title: Twenty-three distinct inline alert geometries across 53 files, with four radii, three border opacities and two off-scale background opacities, because there is no Alert primitive
category: one-off components / inline alerts (53 files across app/ and components/, no primitive in components/ui/)
description: components/ui/ has no alert.tsx. 53 files hand-roll the inline error banner. Extracting every className that pairs a destructive border with a destructive background and has padding and a radius gives 23 unique strings, including: `rounded-md border border-destructive/30 bg-destructive/10 px-3 py-2 text-sm text-destructive`, `rounded-lg border border-destructive/30 bg-destructive/10 px-3 py-2 ...`, `rounded-lg border border-destructive/25 bg-destructive/5 px-3.5 py-3 ...`, `rounded-lg border border-destructive/20 bg-destructive/5 px-3 py-2.5`, `flex items-start gap-3 p-4 rounded-xl border border-destructive/30 bg-destructive/10` (app/teams/page.tsx:518), `rounded-xl border border-destructive/25 bg-destructive/3 p-4 sm:p-5`, `p-4 rounded-2xl mb-5 bg-destructive/10 text-destructive` and `flex flex-col gap-3 rounded-lg border border-destructive/30 bg-destructive/6 p-4`. Radius spans rounded-md, rounded-lg, rounded-xl and rounded-2xl; border opacity spans /20, /25 and /30; background spans /3, /5, /6 and /10; padding spans p-3, p-4, px-3 py-2, px-3 py-2.5, px-3.5 py-3 and px-4 py-3. bg-destructive/3 and bg-destructive/6 are not steps on Tailwind's opacity scale, so they are one-off arbitrary values. The success side has the same problem plus a second syntax split: `bg-[hsl(var(--success)/0.1)]` and `bg-[hsl(var(--success))]/10` both appear for the same colour, and the success banner exists at rounded-md and rounded-lg with px-3 py-2, px-3 py-2.5 and px-3.5 py-3. AUDIT-013#dup-14 filed the state-management half of this (50 components hand-roll a useState banner pair while a full Radix toast stack serves one consumer); this is the visual half and it stands whichever way that decision goes.
impact: Error and success feedback is the highest-stakes UI in the product because it appears when something has gone wrong, and it looks different on every screen it appears on. Nothing signals "this is the app telling you something" consistently. A designer changing the error treatment has to touch 53 files and will miss some, and the two off-scale opacities mean two of the banners are already a shade nobody chose deliberately.
recommendation: Add components/shared/inline-alert.tsx exporting `InlineAlert({ tone, title, children, onDismiss })` with tone in error | success | warning | info. One geometry: `flex items-start gap-2.5 rounded-lg border px-3.5 py-3 text-sm`. One tone table using the dsn-01 foreground tokens: error `border-destructive/30 bg-destructive/10 text-[hsl(var(--destructive-text))]`, success `border-[hsl(var(--success))]/30 bg-[hsl(var(--success))]/10 text-[hsl(var(--success-text))]`, warning `border-[hsl(var(--warning))]/30 bg-[hsl(var(--warning))]/10 text-[hsl(var(--warning-text))]`, info `border-primary/25 bg-primary/5 text-foreground`. Include the leading lucide icon (AlertTriangle / Check / AlertTriangle / Info) and role="alert" so every call site gets the announcement free. Migrate in batches by directory, starting with components/profile (the setError/setSuccess tree at components/profile/types.ts already threads one pair everywhere, so it is the cheapest) and app/teams/page.tsx:518, app/profile/page.tsx:695, app/repos/page.tsx:333 and app/attack-surface/page.tsx:45. Standardise the token syntax on `bg-[hsl(var(--success))]/10` (Tailwind opacity modifier) rather than the two-syntax mix, and delete the bg-destructive/3 and bg-destructive/6 arbitrary values.

title: Seven visual treatments for a row of tabs, only two of which use the Radix Tabs primitive, and /profile's sidebar is /admin's with the focus ring removed
description: Extends AUDIT-011#prof-01 (which filed /profile's mobile tab strip for having no accessible name below 640px) with the rest of the class. Seven treatments: (1) components/ui/tabs.tsx:16-33, a segmented control on `bg-muted p-1` with an active `bg-background shadow-xs` at rounded-sm, h-10, px-3 py-1.5, imported by exactly two files (components/admin/features/ip-rules-manager.tsx:29 and system-settings-manager.tsx:12); (2) components/scanner/issue-detail.tsx:896-916, the same idiom hand-rolled at a different size, `flex gap-1 rounded-md bg-muted p-1` with active `bg-card shadow-xs`, rounded, px-2.5 py-1, text-xs; (3) app/assets/page.tsx:160-183, a third segmented variant, `inline-flex rounded-md border border-border bg-card p-0.5` with active `bg-primary text-primary-foreground`, a solid brand fill where the other two use a neutral raise; (4) components/history/history-view-tabs.tsx:29-44, underline tabs, `flex gap-1 border-b border-border/50` with `-mb-px border-b-2 border-primary px-3 py-2`, and no role or aria-current at all since they are Links; (5) components/docs/docs-code-tabs.tsx:30-47, underline plus fill plus top radius, `rounded-t-lg` with active `bg-secondary/30 border-b-2 border-primary`, px-4 py-2; (6) app/profile/page.tsx:723-739, the mobile strip, underline again but at px-3.5 py-3 with a `border-b border-border/80` rail rather than /50; (7) app/profile/page.tsx:743-768 and app/admin/page.tsx:1052-1097, the desktop vertical sidebar, `bg-primary/10 text-primary font-medium` pills at rounded-lg. Treatment (7) is nearly the same code twice: admin uses px-2.5 py-2 and includes `focus-visible:outline-hidden focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-ring` at :1076; profile uses px-3 py-2.5 and has no focus classes at all, so on /profile the eight sidebar links receive no visible focus except whatever the global :focus-visible rule at app/globals.css:370 supplies, and the sidebar widths differ (lg:w-48 versus lg:w-52).
impact: Tabs are the primary navigation idiom of the signed-in product and there is no such thing as "a tab" here. /assets renders its scope toggle as a solid blue pill, which under design-language.md's accent-restraint doctrine spends the page's one accent on a filter switch; two segmented controls that are visually the same are built two different ways so a keyboard fix lands on one; and the vertical sidebar that /profile and /admin share was copied rather than extracted, which is how /profile lost the explicit focus ring.
recommendation: Two shared components, not seven. (a) components/shared/segmented-control.tsx wrapping Radix Tabs with the components/ui/tabs.tsx:16 geometry plus a size prop ("sm" giving px-2.5 py-1 text-xs for dense use); replace components/scanner/issue-detail.tsx:896 and app/assets/page.tsx:160 with it, and change the assets active state from bg-primary to the neutral `bg-background shadow-xs` raise the primitive already uses. (b) components/shared/section-nav.tsx holding the vertical sidebar markup currently duplicated at app/profile/page.tsx:743 and app/admin/page.tsx:1052, taking `items`, `groups` and `width`, with admin's focus-visible classes and admin's px-2.5 py-2, and use it on both pages. Keep the underline treatment for cross-page navigation only (components/history/history-view-tabs.tsx), give it `aria-current="page"` on the active Link, and switch components/docs/docs-code-tabs.tsx to the same underline geometry (drop rounded-t-lg and bg-secondary/30) so there is one underline tab and one segmented tab in the whole product. AUDIT-011#docs-11's tabpanel/aria-controls fix should land on (a) once, not on each copy.

title: Two callout components with overlapping variant names map warning to two different colours and use border-2, a width used nowhere else in the system
description:
components/docs/docs-callout.tsx:22-47 and components/legal/legal-callout.tsx:10-26 are two callout components with a `variant` prop whose vocabularies overlap but do not match: docs has info | warning | success | error, legal has warning | danger | info. `warning` exists in both and resolves to different colours: docs uses --warning (38 degrees) at :34-36, legal uses --severity-medium (45 degrees) at :12-14. `error` and `danger` are the same thing under two names. The geometry is unrelated too: docs is `rounded-r-lg border border-l-4 border-border/50 p-4` with a coloured left rule, a 3.5 icon and a text-xs font-semibold label, and its docblock at :14-19 explains the choice ("the left rule does the work; there is no icon-in-a-rounded-square, because four of those down a page is decoration"). Legal is `max-w-prose rounded-xl border-2 p-5` with no icon and a text-base font-semibold h3. border-2 appears on exactly one other non-decorative element in app/ and components/ (an avatar ring and a spinner), so it is a one-off width. Both are correct on tokens, so this is purely a grammar split. It also produces a heading-level inconsistency: the legal callout emits an

inside legal sections that already have their own h3s, while the docs callout emits a

.
impact: A reader who goes from /docs/self-hosting (which uses the docs callout heavily) to /legal/acceptable-use sees the same kind of aside drawn with a different border weight, a different radius, no icon and no coloured rule, and the warning aside changes hue. The duplicated vocabulary also means a future "add a note about X" ticket gets two different implementations depending on which directory it lands in.
recommendation:
Delete components/legal/legal-callout.tsx and re-export DocsCallout from components/shared/callout.tsx (moved out of components/docs/ since two sections use it), mapping the two legal call sites: app/legal/acceptable-use/page.tsx:51 variant="warning" stays warning, app/legal/dmca/page.tsx:62 variant="info" stays info, and app/security/page.tsx:63 variant="info" stays info. Keep the docs geometry and the four-variant vocabulary (info | warning | success | error), since it is the one with a written rationale and 60-odd call sites. Add an optional `as="h3"` prop if a legal callout genuinely needs to be a heading in the document outline; otherwise leave it as the

label the docs version uses. Retire the name `danger`.

title: The profile Social tab and the two OAuth profile modals are a brand-chrome island: full-bleed vendor gradients, decorative white blobs, text-white and font-bold, unlike anything else in the app
description: components/profile/tabs/profile-social-tab.tsx:604 opens the Discord card with `relative bg-linear-to-br from-[#5865F2] via-[#4752C4] to-[#3C45A5] px-6 py-5` and :777 opens the GitHub card with `relative bg-linear-to-br from-[#24292e] via-[#1b1f23] to-[#0d1117] px-6 py-5`, both with `titleClassName="text-white"` and `subtitleClassName="text-white/70"`, a `h-10 w-10 rounded-xl bg-white` icon plate at :154, a `bg-white/15 backdrop-blur-xs ring-1 ring-white/20` plate at :607 and a `bg-white/20 text-white border-white/30` badge at :622. components/modals/discord-profile-modal.tsx:90-125 and components/modals/github-profile-modal.tsx:97-125 go further: a full-bleed brand header, three absolutely positioned `rounded-full bg-white/20` decorative circles at :92-94 and :99-101, a `border-4 border-background ring-4` avatar at :120, `text-xl font-bold text-white` at :107 and `text-2xl font-bold` at :125. Nowhere else in app/ or components/ is there a gradient header, a decorative blob, a border-4 ring or text-white outside a scrim. The rest of the product paints on bg-card with a border and spends colour on one element per section. The literal hexes are legitimate third-party brand colours (design-language.md A3 permits them), so the problem is not the values, it is the composition: five nested branded surfaces to say "you can sign in with Discord".
impact: /profile is one of the two or three most-visited signed-in pages, and its Social tab looks like a different design system dropped into a slot. The gradient headers also make the two cards the loudest thing on a page whose actual content (2FA, API keys, billing) is quieter, so visual weight is inverted against importance. The three floating white circles are pure decoration in a product whose illustration doctrine (design-language.md E2) is "the actual mechanism of the product, rendered as itself".
recommendation: Bring both cards back to the house grammar and keep the brand colour as a single accent. Replace the gradient header at profile-social-tab.tsx:604 and :777 with the standard card header used elsewhere in the tab tree, `flex items-center gap-3 border-b border-border/60 px-5 py-4`, holding a `h-9 w-9 rounded-lg` plate filled with the vendor colour (bg-[#5865F2] / bg-[#181717]) and the vendor glyph in white, then `text-base font-semibold text-foreground` for the label and `text-xs text-muted-foreground` for the subtitle; that keeps the brand recognisable in exactly one element per card. Drop titleClassName / subtitleClassName / headerClassName from the OAuthIdentityCard props entirely once both callers stop overriding them. Keep the connect button's brand fill at :721 and :780 (it is the one action that should read as the vendor's) but drop shadow-xs. In components/modals/discord-profile-modal.tsx and github-profile-modal.tsx, delete the six decorative `bg-white/20` circles at :92-94 and :99-101, replace the gradient header with the same bordered header, change `text-xl font-bold text-white` to `text-lg font-semibold text-foreground` and `border-4 ... ring-4` to `ring-2 ring-border`.

title: One static OG image serves every page on the site, so a shared scan, a check page and the pricing page all unfurl identically
description: app/layout.tsx:69-84 is the only `openGraph` block in the entire app/ tree (verified by grep across app/ for both .ts and .tsx), and it points every page at the single static `/og-image.png` built by scripts/build-og-image.mjs from public/og-image.svg. There are zero `opengraph-image.tsx` or `twitter-image.tsx` route files anywhere under app/. That means /shared/[token], /host/[hostname], /compare, /pricing, all 20 /docs sections and the roughly 750 /checks SEO pages every unfurl with the same card, whose baked copy reads "Scan any website for security issues in seconds. Just a URL." over a mock result for "your-domain.com" showing a risk score of 2 and five invented findings. The card itself is strong work (audits/AUDIT-011/design-language.md names it one of the three best artifacts in the repo) and it is right for the site root, but it is the only card that exists.
impact: Sharing a scan is a core flow, and the share link is the product's main organic distribution: a user pastes /shared/<token> into a Slack channel or a ticket, and everyone who sees it gets a generic marketing card for a fictional domain instead of the hostname and the finding counts they were being shown. The same applies to the roughly 750 /checks pages, which are the main organic SEO surface: every one of them competes for the same unfurl, so nothing in a search or social preview distinguishes "Missing HSTS" from "Exposed .git directory". This compounds AUDIT-012#fe-01, which already found only 5 of 311 routes prerendered.
recommendation: Add three `opengraph-image.tsx` route files using next/og ImageResponse, all rendering one shared layout so they read as a family with the existing SVG (bg #0a0e18 to #0e1526, card #141d30, stroke #26344d, mono wordmark top-left, headline in #ffffff with the accent clause in #60a5fa, severity dots straight from the --severity-* scale exactly as og-image.svg:93-101 already does). (1) app/shared/[token]/opengraph-image.tsx: the scanned hostname as the headline, the risk score chip, and one severity distribution bar with the real counts, all read from the same share query the page uses. (2) app/checks/[slug]/opengraph-image.tsx: the check title, its severity chip, and its category, from the checks registry. (3) app/host/[hostname]/opengraph-image.tsx: the hostname and its current reputation score. Set `export const size = { width: 1200, height: 630 }` and `alt` on each. Keep the static PNG as the root and docs fallback. Because ImageResponse only supports a subset of CSS, build it as flex boxes with explicit widths, and load no external font: the site already ships in system-ui (AUDIT-011#design-02), so next/og's default is consistent with the product rather than a deviation.

title: app/global-error.tsx is a different design from the other two error pages: different palette, no wordmark, no status numeral, no digest, and no light mode
description: app/error.tsx and app/not-found.tsx are the same composition: a mono wordmark lockup with ThemedLogo, a `border-y border-border/50 py-8` band holding a `font-mono text-6xl font-semibold tabular-nums` status numeral (500 / 404), a short honest sentence, a two-up button row, and a row of three or two `text-primary` footer links, all on tokens and all with `focus.ring` (error.tsx:33-127, not-found.tsx:15-89). app/global-error.tsx shares none of it: it opens with a 6rem circle holding a warning icon at :51-60 (an icon-in-a-rounded-shape, which CLAUDE.md and design-language E1 name as an anti-pattern), has no wordmark at all, no numeral, no error.digest block despite error.digest being available in its props, and it hardcodes `#09090b` / `#fafafa` / `#a1a1aa` / `#71717a` / `#52525b`, which is the Tailwind zinc ramp, not the app's #0C0E12 / #F0F2F5 navy. Its two links are coloured `BRAND_TEAL = "#0891b2"` (:10), a brand the product no longer has. It is also dark-only: a light-mode user hitting the global boundary drops into a black page. Inline styles there are correct and the file's own comment (:6-9) explains why, but the values are wrong, and nothing forces the two files to stay in sync. Separately, both error.tsx:103 and not-found.tsx:47 label the secondary route back as "Go to Dashboard", which is the product's internal noun for what an anonymous visitor arriving on a 404 from a search engine experiences as the scan page.
impact: The global boundary is the page a user sees when the app has failed hardest, and it is the one that looks least like the product: teal links on zinc, no logo, no error id to quote to support. A user who does reach it cannot copy a digest, so a support conversation starts with "it broke" and no correlation id. The publicly reachable and indexable 404 sends an anonymous visitor to a button labelled with a word that only means something to an existing user.
recommendation: Rebuild app/global-error.tsx as a literal-hex mirror of app/error.tsx rather than a separate design. Keep the inline-style constraint, but source the values from lib/config/brand.ts by transcribing them with a comment pointing back: background #0b0e14, card #12151c, border #252a34, text #f1f5f9, muted #9aa6b8, link #60a5fa (delete BRAND_TEAL). Add a `@media (prefers-color-scheme: light)` block via a small inline `<style>` element in the same file so the light palette (#dfe5ec / #eff2f5 / #14181f) is available without CSS variables. Replace the 6rem icon circle with the same structure error.tsx uses: an inline SVG VulnRadar mark plus the wordmark in `ui-monospace` at 20px/600, a 1px top and bottom rule at rgba(255,255,255,0.08), a monospace 60px "500", the heading "Something broke on our end", and the digest in a bordered mono block with a copy button (navigator.clipboard, guarded). Add a comment in both files naming the other as the sibling that must match. Separately, change the secondary CTA label in both error.tsx:105 and not-found.tsx:49 from "Go to Dashboard" to "Scan a URL", which is what the page actually does and matches the voice rule that copy names the mechanism.

title: API_VERSION exists so "all API calls" can be switched between versions, but 60 fetch call sites across 28 files hardcode the /api/v3 path instead
description: lib/config/client-constants.ts:80-83 declares `// API VERSION - Change this to switch all API calls between versions` followed by `export const API_VERSION = "v3"`, and :87 onwards builds the whole API route map from it as template literals. That map is used correctly 157 times across app/ and components/. It is also bypassed 60 times in 28 files by fetches that spell the version out: app/admin/page.tsx alone has five (:350, :447, :456, :468, :489), plus app/admin/ai-chats/[id]/page.tsx:73, app/checkout/browser-credits/page.tsx:35, app/checkout/credits/page.tsx:34, app/checkout/github-credits/page.tsx:36, app/checkout/[productId]/page.tsx:55, app/dashboard/page.tsx:273 and app/unsubscribe/page.tsx:197 among others. lib/config/config-values.ts:659-660 additionally exports CONFIG_API_CURRENT_VERSION and CONFIG_API_SUPPORTED_VERSIONS as a second, unconnected copy of the same fact.
impact: The stated purpose of the constant is not achievable: bumping API_VERSION to v4 leaves 60 client calls pointed at v3, so the app would half-migrate with no compile error and no test failure, and the breakage would surface as scattered 404s in admin, checkout, dashboard and unsubscribe. This is the reverse-check shape the section is about: the operator or maintainer believes they changed one value and changed 72 percent of the call sites. Not self-host-breaking today, since v3 is the only supported version, but it makes the one migration the constant exists for unsafe.
recommendation: Add the missing routes to the API map in lib/config/client-constants.ts:87 onwards (admin teams, admin updater status, ai conversations, ai info, auth me is already there, account unsubscribe) and replace the 60 literals with the map entries. Then add an ESLint `no-restricted-syntax` rule scoped to app/ and components/ that flags any string literal matching `/api/v\d`, so the 61st cannot be added silently. Also collapse CONFIG_API_CURRENT_VERSION into API_VERSION so there is one source of truth rather than two.

title: The self-updater advertises itself as supported inside Docker but writes into a root-owned /app as uid 1001, runs a migrate script the image does not contain, and any success is discarded by the documented update command
description: Static trace. isUpdaterSupported() (lib/updater/environment.ts:8-17) returns unsupported only when process.env.VERCEL is set; there is no container detection, so both app/api/v3/admin/updater/status/route.ts:37 and .../apply/route.ts:56 report the updater available inside the official image and the admin UI offers it. runUpdateJob then sets appRoot = process.cwd() (lib/updater/apply.ts:206), which is /app, and calls copyTreeOverlay(sourceRoot, appRoot) at :261 to write the release's full source tree there. /app is root:root because WORKDIR /app runs as root at Dockerfile:68 and the process runs as USER nextjs (uid 1001) from :102, so creating new top-level entries such as /app/lib or /app/app fails with EACCES, while pre-existing chowned files such as /app/package.json and /app/next.config.mjs would be overwritten in place first (overwriting an existing file needs write on the file, not the directory). The job then fails with a raw permission error after package.json has already been replaced with the new release's copy while node_modules and .next are still the old build. Even if the copy succeeded, the npm-ci step at :325 and the `npm run db:migrate -- --yes` step at :353 run against a tree with no scripts/ (host-02), and the final log line at :369 asks the admin to run `npm run build` and restart, which in a container means the next `docker compose pull && docker compose up -d` (app/docs/setup/page.tsx:684) throws the whole writable layer away. AUDIT-013#cov-06 recorded that this pipeline has 0% test coverage and AUDIT-013#migrate-01 that the migrate step it invokes stamps 3.0.0 on a schema missing 11 tables; this finding is about the updater being reachable at all in the deployment shape where it cannot work.
impact: A self-hosting admin sees an in-app Update button, clicks it, and gets a half-applied file copy plus an opaque EACCES in the job log, with package.json now describing a version whose code is not installed. In the worst case they then follow the log's advice and restart, and the update silently disappears on the next image pull.
recommendation: Extend isUpdaterSupported() in lib/updater/environment.ts to detect a container (existence of /.dockerenv, or an explicit CONTAINER/VULNRADAR_UPDATER_DISABLED env var set in the Dockerfile) and return supported: false with a reason pointing at `docker compose pull`. If in-container updating is wanted instead, chown /app to nextjs:nodejs in the runner stage and ship scripts/ (host-02).

title: The admin 'update password' action enforces a hardcoded 8-character minimum, bypassing the admin-configurable PASSWORD_MIN_LENGTH (12) and the strength gate every user-facing path applies
description: Every user-facing password path resolves the live setting and then runs the strength analyzer: app/api/v3/auth/signup/route.ts:68-:72 and :88-:89, app/api/v3/auth/reset-password/route.ts:36-:41 and :46-:47, app/api/v3/auth/update/route.ts:316 and :301-:302, app/api/v3/auth/staff-invite/[token]/route.ts:156 and :170-:171. All four call getSetting('PASSWORD_MIN_LENGTH') (default CONFIG_PASSWORD_MIN_LENGTH = 12, lib/config/config-values.ts:314, admin-editable at lib/config/registry.ts:2130) and reject analyzePassword(pw).score < 3. The admin case 'update_password' at app/api/v3/admin/route.ts:732-:753 does neither: it validates only `typeof newPassword !== 'string' || newPassword.length < 8`, hashes, writes, and revokes sessions. There is no getSetting call and no analyzePassword call anywhere in that branch.
impact: On a deployment where the operator raised PASSWORD_MIN_LENGTH to meet a policy, an admin resetting a user's password can still set an 8-character password, and 'Password123' passes because the analyzer never runs. The account then holds a credential the deployment's own configured policy forbids, and the audit log records it as a normal update_password action.
recommendation: In app/api/v3/admin/route.ts's update_password case, replace the literal 8 with `await getSetting('PASSWORD_MIN_LENGTH')` and add the same `analyzePassword(newPassword).score < 3` rejection the other four routes use, so all five password write paths share one policy.

title: Both user-visible scoring engines, the safety verdict and the SSL letter grade, are built entirely from unnamed literals with zero registry entries, so the false-positive rate is untunable
description: getSafetyRating decides safe/caution/unsafe from four bare comparisons: criticalExploitWeight >= 1 (:260), highExploitWeight >= 2 (:264), mediumExploitWeight >= 3 (:276), highHardeningWeight >= 5 (:282). getDangerScore adds SEVERITY_WEIGHTS critical 4 / high 2 / medium 1 / low 0.3 / info 0.05 (:298-:304), the tierBase and tierCap tables (:312-:321), a fallback weight of 0.1 (:327), and the multipliers 1.5 exploitable / 0.15 hardening / 0.05 other (:335-:337). getEngineConfidence adds a base of 97, a 94 timed-out variant (:368), a per-severity averaging table (:373-:379), a default confidence of 85 for a finding that carries none (:385), and a 0.3/0.7 blend with a floor of 50 (:392-:394). lib/scanner/ssl-grade.ts is the same story: deductions of 55, 70, 40, 20, 10 and 5, bonuses of 3, and the letter cutoffs 95/80/65/50/35 at :231-:236. A grep of lib/config/registry.ts for 'safety', 'danger' or 'confidence' returns only the three ADAPTIVE_CONFIDENCE / ENGINE_FEEDBACK entries (registry.ts:2731-2751), none of which touch any of the numbers above. The per-check static confidence values are equally scattered as literals across roughly 40 files (lib/scanner/checks/page-checks/links.ts:124 confidence 45, disclosure.ts:135 confidence 55, framework-fingerprint.ts:111 confidence 92, and so on).
impact: An operator running VulnRadar against a fleet where five missing hardening headers is normal has no way to stop every host being labelled 'caution'; the only lever the admin panel offers is turning adaptive confidence on or off. A security team that wants a stricter or looser bar has to fork lib/scanner/safety-rating.ts, which puts them off the upgrade path for a scanner whose whole value is the checks it ships.
recommendation: Name and export the four getSafetyRating comparison thresholds and the two ssl-grade letter tables as CONFIG_ constants in lib/config/config-values.ts and register them in lib/config/registry.ts under the existing scanner section, the same way SCANNER_THREAT_INTEL_API_TIMEOUT_MS and ENGINE_FEEDBACK_NOISE_THRESHOLD_PERCENT already are. The scoring weights themselves can stay as named constants without registry entries; the tier boundaries are the ones an operator actually needs.

title: Four security-relevant rate limits are inline numeric literals that never reach the admin registry, unlike the seventeen that do
description: lib/rate-limiting/rate-limit.ts:247-:276 exposes seventeen named rate limits, each carrying a `limit` name so checkRateLimit resolves the live admin override (registry keys RATE_LIMIT_*_MAX_ATTEMPTS / _WINDOW_MINUTES). Four call sites bypass that entirely by passing raw numbers: app/api/v3/auth/forgot-password/route.ts:49-:53 (per-email reset cap, maxAttempts 3 / windowSeconds 60*60), app/api/v3/auth/signup/route.ts:130-:134 (per-email signup cap, 5 / 60*60), app/api/v3/domains/route.ts:69-:73 (domain add, 20 / 3600) and app/api/v3/domains/[id]/verify/route.ts:39-:42 (domain verify, 30 / 3600). None of the four has a registry key. This is distinct from AUDIT-009#dup-01, which was about routes importing the wrong RATE_LIMITS export; lib/config/constants.ts:352-:360 records that collision as resolved. These four never reference either export.
impact: An operator responding to a signup-flood or reset-flood incident can tighten every limiter in the admin panel and still leave the two per-email counters, which are the ones that actually stop the attack described in each site's own comment, at their compiled values. The two domain limiters are the documented numbers in app/docs/api/page.tsx:843 and :876, so the docs also become uneditable truth.
recommendation: Add four entries to RATE_LIMIT_DEFAULTS and RATE_LIMITS (forgotPasswordEmail, signupEmail, domainAdd, domainVerify) in lib/rate-limiting/rate-limit.ts with matching registry keys, then spread them at the four call sites the way every other limiter does.

title: The CLI's default 300-second timeout is the single-scan budget, so `vulnradar scan --crawl` in CI exits 1 as 'Timed out' on a crawl the server still has 600 seconds left to finish
description: cli/lib.mjs:5-:14 declares DEFAULTS with `timeout: 300` and `crawl: false`. cli/vulnradar.mjs:64 turns that into `const deadline = Date.now() + opts.timeout * 1000` and the poll loop at :65-:85 gives up at the deadline, printing 'Timed out after 300s waiting for scan ${scanId}.' at :88-:90 and calling process.exit(1) at :91. Server-side, 300 is exactly CONFIG_SCAN_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (lib/config/config-values.ts:544) for a single-URL scan, but a crawl runs under CONFIG_CRAWL_SCAN_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 900 (:551), enforced by the crawl watchdog at lib/scanner/execute-crawl-scan.ts:361-:364. The CLI passes --crawl through but never adjusts its own deadline, and neither cli/lib.mjs:130 ('Give up waiting for the scan (default 300)') nor app/docs/cli/page.tsx:135 and :154 warns that --crawl needs a larger --timeout.
impact: A CI job that runs `vulnradar scan --crawl` against a site of any size fails red on a scan that is still running and will complete successfully. The user sees a timeout error, the pipeline blocks the merge, and the scan quietly finishes and lands in history a few minutes later, which reads as the tool being unreliable rather than as a default being wrong.
recommendation: In cli/lib.mjs, make the effective default conditional on the crawl flag (300 for a single scan, 900 for --crawl) while still honouring an explicit --timeout, and say so in the --timeout help text at :130 and in app/docs/cli/page.tsx's flag table.

title: The web surface ships zero screenshots of the application, and the five finished 533x333 store screenshots in extension/public/store are referenced by no page, route, or asset in the repo
description: Grepping app/, components/, public/, lib/ and scripts/ for "store_" returns zero matches outside extension/public/store itself, so store_1.png through store_5.png are used only in the Chrome Web Store and AMO listings. public/ contains exactly six files (favicon.ico, favicon.png, favicon.svg, gitlab, og-image.png, og-image.svg) and no product imagery. components/landing/ and app/landing/ contain zero next/image imports, zero , and zero .png/.jpg/.webp references. What the landing page does show is genuinely good and should not be discarded: components/shared/response-readout.tsx renders a live request/response readout in the hero, and components/landing/landing-sample-finding.tsx:59-107 hand-builds a complete finding card in JSX with real evidence and a real Nginx and Express fix. So the gap is not "the output is never shown", the output is shown well. The gap is that nothing shows the application: the dashboard, the history list, the two-scan diff at /compare that components/landing/landing-features.tsx:34-36 leans on as its closing argument, or the extension that is live on two stores. The five unused PNGs are, per audits/AUDIT-011/design-language.md section E3, one of the three strongest visual artefacts in the repo, with an established composition (alternating side, two-tone white and #60a5fa headline, mono footnote, real UI over a browser-chrome mock).
impact: A security scanner's report is its product, and a visitor deciding between this and a commercial scanner has no way to see whether the application is a real product or a landing page with an API behind it. Trust for an unknown vendor with roughly 50 users is bought largely with evidence that the thing exists. Meanwhile finished, on-brand art that cost real design effort reaches only Chrome Web Store browsers and never the site.
recommendation: Copy extension/public/store/*.png to public/store/ and add five specific images to the web surface.
