(1) A full completed report from /dashboard, placed as a full-bleed band directly after the hero, showing the verdict header, the SeverityDistribution bar from components/scanner/severity-badge.tsx:129-190, and the first four findings collapsed. This is the missing "the product exists" proof. (2) A real screenshot of IssueDetail expanded on hsts-missing, replacing the hand-built <article> at landing-sample-finding.tsx:59-107 while keeping its left column copy verbatim: the JSX version is a drawing of the product, the screenshot is the product. (3) The /compare two-scan diff, added as a small figure inside components/landing/landing-features.tsx's accent block, because "what makes the diff between Tuesday and Friday readable" (:34-36) is the one claim the page argues hardest and never shows. (4) store_1.png reused as-is on a new /extension marketing page and in app/docs/extension/page.tsx. (5) The dashboard scan form with the category selector open, next to landing-categories.tsx:30-32's claim that checks are gated to the URL types they apply to. Use next/image with explicit width and height, wrap each in a rounded-xl border border-border/60 to match the card grammar in design-language.md D1, and give each a real alt describing the finding shown, not "screenshot".

title: Plan copy sells raw numbers and platitudes instead of what a user can do, and the checkout page advertises a 30 and 90 day scan history that no plan actually has
description: lib/billing/catalog.ts descriptions are the copy that appears under each plan name at components/pricing/pricing-cards.tsx:83-85: "For individuals exploring security scanning" (:103), "Support VulnRadar development + 100 scans/day" (:133), "For power users - 150 scans/day" (:166), "Maximum power - 500 scans/day" (:198). "For power users" and "Maximum power" are exactly the adjective-only benefit claims CLAUDE.md bans, and none of the four says what the extra scans let you do. The feature bullets are the same shape: "Full vulnerability detection", "Security headers analysis", "SSL/TLS checks", "API access" (:106-109) are category nouns with no consequence attached, and every one of them is true on every plan, so the free card spends four of its eight bullets on things that are not differentiators. Separately there is a factual error. CONFIG_BILLING_FREE_RETENTION through CONFIG_BILLING_ELITE_SUPPORTER_RETENTION are all -1, meaning unlimited (lib/config/config-values.ts:1209-1212), yet catalog.ts:110 still says "30-day scan history" and :137 says "90-day scan history". app/pricing/page.tsx:44 strips those strings with a /scan history/i filter, but app/checkout/[productId]/page.tsx:280 renders plan.features.slice(0, 5) with no filter, so the Core checkout page, the highest-intent page in the funnel, tells a buyer they are getting 90-day history when every plan including free already keeps everything. catalog.ts:170 then sells "Unlimited scan history" as a Pro upgrade over Core, which the free tier also has. Finally components/pricing/pricing-cards.tsx:78-79 renders a "Most picked" badge driven by the hardcoded `popular: libPlan.id === "pro_supporter"` at app/pricing/page.tsx:55, which is a claim about other customers' behaviour that is not measured from anything.
impact: A visitor cannot tell what changes when they pay, because the cards restate the same nouns at four price points and the one concrete difference they do state, retention, is wrong on the checkout page and identical across plans in reality. The Pro card's headline upgrade is something the free tier already includes. "Most picked" is an unbacked social-proof claim on a product with roughly 50 users, which is the kind of thing that is cheap to remove and expensive if noticed.
recommendation: Rewrite the four descriptions in lib/billing/catalog.ts in terms of what the tier lets you do: free (:103) "25 scans a day. Enough to keep an eye on everything you personally ship." core_supporter (:133) "100 scans a day and two running at once, for someone watching more than one property." pro_supporter (:166) "150 scans a day, a team of three, and 5,000 API calls a day. Enough to gate a real pipeline." elite_supporter (:198) "500 scans a day, unlimited webhooks and schedules, teams of ten. For an agency or a portfolio." Rewrite the free bullets (:105-114) to "Every check on every plan, nothing held back behind a tier", "25 scans a day, one at a time", "Unlimited history, diff any two runs", "5 URLs per bulk call, 3 schedules, 1 webhook", "REST API and one bearer token", "PDF, JSON, SARIF and Markdown export". Delete the "30-day scan history" string at :110 and "90-day scan history" at :137 outright so getRetentionLabel in app/pricing/page.tsx:26-31 is the only source, which also repairs the checkout page without touching it, and drop "Unlimited scan history" from the Pro list at :170 since it is not an upgrade. Either replace the "Most picked" badge at components/pricing/pricing-cards.tsx:78-79 with a factual label such as "Recommended", or drive `popular` from a real distribution query.

title: Every honest trust signal the project owns is unlinked from the marketing surface: the public scan directory, the comparison pages, the 754 check pages, the free tools, the security page and the committed audit history
description: What exists and is verifiable: /public-scans, a directory of real scans users chose to publish (app/public-scans/page.tsx, public per lib/config/public-paths.ts); /alternatives, five honest comparison pages whose own copy commits to "No invented competitor prices, no disparagement" (app/alternatives/page.tsx:47-48); roughly 754 /checks pages, each a real rule with its own fix guide; /tools, two free tools; /security plus /.well-known/security.txt; SECURITY-POSTURE.md, a public self-hardening checklist that opens with "We ship a scanner that grades other people's domains, so our own domain has to pass its own checks"; a live dogfood badge in README.md:18 pointing at a permanent shared report of vulnradar.dev; fourteen self-audits committed in audits/ (verified tracked with git ls-files, not ignored); a changelog; GPL-3.0; "Telemetry: None"; two live store listings. What links to any of it from the marketing surface: grepping components/landing/, app/landing/ and components/scanner/footer.tsx for "/checks", "/public-scans", "PUBLIC_SCANS", "/alternatives" and "/tools" returns zero matches. /public-scans is linked only from components/scanner/header.tsx (the logged-in app header) and two docs pages. components/scanner/footer.tsx:60-107's Product column lists Scanner, History, Compare and Badges, of which Scanner and History both require a session, so a logged-out visitor's footer is mostly redirects to /login. components/landing/landing-categories.tsx renders all eighteen categories as a table with counts and blurbs and not one cell is a link, so the highest-authority page on the site sends no traffic and no link equity into the 754-page check surface it is describing.
impact: For a security product from an unknown vendor, trust is the purchase. This project has an unusually strong honest-signal inventory for its size, including a committed audit history and a published self-hardening checklist, and a visitor is shown none of it. Separately, the roughly 780 SEO pages have no inbound link from the landing page, so the main organic surface is orphaned from the site's strongest page.
recommendation: Do not invent social proof, surface what exists. (1) Make every category row in components/landing/landing-categories.tsx link to /checks/category/{key}, both in the sm:hidden card list at :42-79 and the table at :81-146, and add a "See all {total} checks" link to /checks beside the count at :34-39. That is eighteen internal links from the site's strongest page into the SEO surface, and it makes the section clickable proof rather than a static table. (2) Add a Resources footer entry for /public-scans labelled "Public scans" and one for /alternatives labelled "Compared to other scanners", and a Product entry for /tools labelled "Free tools", in components/scanner/footer.tsx:60-150. (3) Extend the FACTS <dl> in components/landing/landing-open-source.tsx:6-13 with two rows that are the strongest available and currently invisible: ["Our own last scan", "Public, permanent report"] linking the shared report README.md:18 already uses, and ["Self-audits", "14, committed in the repo"] linking audits/ on GitHub. Verify the shared-report link still resolves before publishing it. (4) Note the honest caveat: /public-scans is opt-in and its empty state (components/public-scans/public-scans-empty-state.tsx:9) says "No public scans yet", so check it has content before linking it from the landing page, and seed it by publishing the team's own scans first.

title: There is no command palette and no keyboard shortcut layer anywhere in a developer tool with eight top-level sections
description: A repo-wide grep for cmdk, CommandDialog, useHotkeys and global keydown handlers finds no command palette and no application-level shortcut registration. The only document-level keydown listeners in app/ and components/ are modal Escape and focus trapping (lib/hooks/use-modal-a11y.ts:54 and :91), the AI chat widget's own textarea handling (components/ai-chat/chat-widget.tsx:833 and :1070), and two mobile nav overlays (components/docs/docs-mobile-nav.tsx:58, components/admin/shared/admin-mobile-toc.tsx:140). There is no global search either: components/scanner/header.tsx renders logo, eight nav links (:25-34), a notification bell, a theme toggle and log out, with no search input at any breakpoint. app/docs has no search of any kind: components/docs/docs-sidebar.tsx and docs-shell.tsx contain no input element.
impact: Reaching a past scan means navigating to History and typing into a filter that only covers the newest 100 rows. Reaching scheduled scans means Profile, then the Developer tab, then the Schedules sub-tab. Reaching one check's documentation means /checks, expanding one of eighteen accordions, then browser find. Each of these is a single fuzzy-search entry for the audience this product targets, and its absence is the most visible way the app reads as less finished than the landing page that sells it.
recommendation: Add a Cmd/Ctrl-K palette mounted next to <Toaster /> in app/layout.tsx. cmdk is the conventional choice and the repo already uses Radix throughout, so components/ui/dialog.tsx supplies the shell. Seed it with five groups: Navigate, from the NAV_LINKS array at components/scanner/header.tsx:25-34 plus the profile tab list at app/profile/page.tsx:625-665; Actions (New scan, Compare scans, New API key, New schedule); Scans, hitting the server-side history search from qolf-01, matched on URL and tag; Checks, over the static registry that already backs app/checks/page.tsx, jumping to /checks/{id}; and Docs, over the tree in components/docs/docs-nav.ts. Then add a shortcut sheet on `?` and the three shortcuts that matter on a results page: `/` to focus the findings search (components/scanner/results-list.tsx:372), j and k to move between findings, Escape to return to the list.

title: There is no undo anywhere in the product, and clearing all history is a single icon button beside the search box
description: A repo-wide grep for undo across app/, components/ and lib/ returns five hits and none is an undo affordance: three are code comments, one is a docs sentence stating there is no undo (app/docs/account-security/page.tsx:503), and one is an unsaved-state toggle label in the admin badge editor (components/admin/users/user-detail-panel.tsx:1198). Every destructive path is therefore confirm-then-permanent. Clear all history deletes every scan on the account in one DELETE (app/history/page.tsx:280-295, dialog :640-694) and its trigger is a single icon button sitting immediately beside the search input in the filter row (components/history/history-filters.tsx:76-88). Delete scan removes the scan, its findings and its notes (components/scanner/scan-actions-menu.tsx:505-515). Remove member, Delete team, Delete schedule and Delete webhook are the same shape (app/teams/page.tsx:340 and :250, components/profile/tabs/profile-developer-tab.tsx:388 and :368).
impact: Clear all history is the one that will eventually cost a user everything they have, and it is two clicks from a control adjacent to the search box they use constantly. For a product whose entire value is that finding IDs are stable across runs so a diff between two scans means something, losing the history destroys the diff, and there is nothing to recover from.
recommendation: Add a soft-delete window for the three that need it most, in this order. (1) Clear all history: add a deleted_at column to scan_history, have the DELETE handler stamp it rather than delete, exclude stamped rows from the list query at app/api/v3/history/route.ts:117-142, and show a persistent "Cleared 143 scans. Undo" bar for 30 seconds after the dialog closes, purging stamped rows on the existing retention sweep. (2) Delete scan: same mechanism surfaced as an undo toast (qolf-07). (3) Remove team member: re-adding is possible via invite but loses their scan association, so stamp and offer undo. Once undo exists for an action, drop that action's confirmation dialog: an undo bar plus an AlertDialog for the same action is one interruption too many. Also move the Clear All button out of the filter row into a danger section below the list, away from the search input it currently sits beside.

title: No search or filter state anywhere in the app is URL-backed, so opening a finding and pressing Back silently resets every filter you set
description: lib/ui/url-state.ts provides a complete solution including the LOCATION_CHANGE_EVENT bridge (:19-49) and a useQueryParam hook (:170), but that hook has only two consumers repo-wide: app/repos/page.tsx:134 and components/profile/tabs/profile-developer-tab.tsx. Everywhere else `page` and `scope` are hand-wired into the URL while every search box and filter is plain useState: components/scanner/results-list.tsx:114-120 (severity set, category, sort direction, grouping, search), app/history/page.tsx:66-67 and :72, app/teams/page.tsx:49, app/assets/page.tsx:35, app/compare/page.tsx:37, app/admin/page.tsx:197. The findings list is the sharp case: selecting a finding calls setQueryParam(FINDING_QUERY_PARAM, issue.id) with the default pushState at components/scanner/results-list.tsx:273, creating a history entry, and both host pages swap ResultsList out for IssueDetail (app/history/page.tsx:465-473). Pressing Back unmounts IssueDetail, remounts ResultsList, and every filter returns to its default at :114-120, while scroll position is deliberately preserved across that same remount at :262-267.
impact: Reviewing a scan goes: filter to Critical and High, open the first finding, read it, press Back, and the list is unfiltered again while the scroll position is restored to where you were in the shorter filtered list, dropping you at an arbitrary offset in a longer one. On a 200-finding crawl that happens on every single finding. Nothing filtered can be shared or bookmarked either: a link to "the criticals on this scan" or "my staging scans" does not exist.
recommendation: Swap the useState declarations for the useQueryParam hook that already exists. In components/scanner/results-list.tsx:114-120 back sev, cat, sort, group and q with query params, omitting each when it equals its default so a clean scan URL stays clean, and write them with { replace: true } so filter changes do not pollute the back stack (the finding param at :273 keeps pushState, which is correct). Do the same for filter and tag in app/history/page.tsx:66-67 and the search state in app/teams/page.tsx:49, app/assets/page.tsx:35 and app/compare/page.tsx:37. Also add LOCATION_CHANGE_EVENT to the two page-sync effects that listen only for QUERY_CHANGE_EVENT and popstate, app/public-scans/page.tsx:99-100 and app/assets/page.tsx:60-61, since clicking their own tab in components/history/history-view-tabs.tsx while already on that page at ?page=3 is exactly the soft-navigation case the bridge was written for and which app/history/page.tsx:213 already handles.

title: There is no path from a finding you just fixed back to verifying it: no rescan on the issue view, and Compare is reachable only from the top nav
description: components/scanner/issue-detail.tsx renders a full remediation lifecycle (Open / In progress / Fixed, persisted at :349 and keyed on the stable finding id per the docblock at :253-259) but contains no action that re-runs the scan or re-checks that finding. The only rescan in the product is the history row menu, which is desktop-only and a no-op (qolf-02, qolf-03). Compare is linked from exactly two places, components/scanner/header.tsx:29 and components/scanner/footer.tsx:85, never from a scan or a finding. Reaching a diff from an open finding is: back to the findings list, back to history, Compare in the nav, find the host in the picker (app/compare/page.tsx:238), pick two scans if the host has more than two (:268), press Compare (:276). Six interactions, and the host you were just looking at is not preselected.
impact: Find, fix, verify is the loop this product exists to serve, and verify is the only leg with no direct route. In practice users mark a finding Fixed and never confirm it, which makes the remediation status a self-reported label rather than a verified one, and leaves the strongest claim the product makes ("the same URL produces the same finding IDs and the same ratings on every run, which is the only reason a diff between two scans means anything", components/landing/landing-how-it-works.tsx:32-35) unreachable from inside the product.
recommendation: Add two entries. First, a "Re-check this" button on the issue detail beside the remediation control at components/scanner/issue-detail.tsx:829: it runs the same scan the dashboard does against result.url, polls status, and on completion reports whether this finding id is present in the new run, then offers "Open the new scan" and "Mark fixed". Second, add "Compare with previous scan" to the scan actions menu (components/scanner/scan-actions-menu.tsx:532-661, beside the existing Share entry), resolving the previous scan for the same host server-side and navigating straight to /compare?a=<prev>&b=<current>, which app/compare/page.tsx:72-93 already accepts as a deep link. Both collapse six interactions to one and both reuse existing endpoints.

title: The Developer nav entry that made scheduled scans discoverable is dead code: DEVELOPER_HREF is not in NAV_LINKS, so 25 lines of header logic can never run
description: components/scanner/header.tsx:23 defines DEVELOPER_HREF as `${ROUTES.PROFILE}?tab=developer` under a comment at :18-22 explaining that scheduled scans, webhooks, domains and API keys "had no top-level entry, so recurring monitoring, the whole point of a scheduled scan, was two clicks deep under Profile and effectively undiscoverable". NAV_LINKS at :25-34 lists eight entries and DEVELOPER_HREF is not one of them. Consequently handleNavClick (:69-79) always returns at its first line `if (href !== DEVELOPER_HREF) return`, because no rendered link ever equals that constant; the `if (href === DEVELOPER_HREF)` branch in isNavActive (:82) is unreachable; and the locationSearch state with its popstate and QUERY_CHANGE_EVENT effect (:45-58) plus the onDeveloperTab derivation (:59-60) exist only to feed that unreachable branch.
impact: Scheduled scans, webhooks, verified domains and API keys are back to three navigations deep with no top-level entry, which the code comment itself identifies as the problem this was supposed to fix. Recurring monitoring is the feature that turns a one-off scanner into something a team keeps paying for, and nothing in the product's chrome points at it. Twenty-five lines of header code also carry maintenance cost and read as intentional to the next person editing the file.
recommendation: Add { href: DEVELOPER_HREF, label: "Developer" } to NAV_LINKS at components/scanner/header.tsx:25-34, which restores every code path in the file. Nine desktop items is one too many for the absolutely-centred nav at :153, so move Badge (:32) into the Developer tab where it belongs, since it is a per-scan embed rather than a section. If the entry is genuinely not wanted, delete DEVELOPER_HREF, handleNavClick, the locationSearch state and effect, and the onDeveloperTab derivation rather than leaving them, and surface schedules another way, for example a "Schedule this scan" entry in the scan actions menu that deep-links to /profile?tab=developer&dtab=schedules with the URL prefilled.

title: No user-facing list in the product has a sort control, and history has no severity, date-range or source filter despite carrying all three fields
description: components/history/history-filters.tsx renders exactly three controls: a URL search box (:36), a tag dropdown (:46) and Clear All (:76). Repo-wide only four files contain any sort state (components/scanner/results-list.tsx, components/admin/features/ai-chats-manager.tsx, components/admin/features/ip-rules-manager.tsx, components/admin/staff/staff-list.tsx) and only the first is on a non-admin surface. Every user list is therefore locked to a fixed server order: history ORDER BY sh.scanned_at DESC (app/api/v3/history/route.ts:127), shares ORDER BY scanned_at DESC (app/api/v3/shares/route.ts:28), assets ORDER BY last_scanned_at DESC (app/api/v3/assets/route.ts:141), public scans ORDER BY sh.scanned_at DESC (app/api/v3/public-scans/route.ts:94). Yet the history row already renders per-severity counts from s.summary (components/history/history-scan-row.tsx:57-72) and the API already selects sh.source (app/api/v3/history/route.ts:119) and never exposes it.
impact: "Show me every scan that turned up a critical" and "show me last week" are the two questions a security team asks of a scan history, and neither is answerable, so triage is scroll-and-read. Two defaults are also on the wrong axis: /shares sorts by when the underlying scan ran rather than when the link was created or expires, and /assets sorts by most-recently-scanned, which surfaces the host you already know about and buries the stale one, when "not scanned in N days" is the single most useful view of an asset inventory.
recommendation: On the history filter row add a severity segmented filter (Any / Critical / High and above / Clean) derived from s.summary, a date-range select (Last 7 days / 30 days / All), a source filter over the source column the API already returns, and a sort select (Newest, Worst severity, Most findings, Host A-Z). Push all of them into SQL alongside the server-side search from qolf-01 rather than filtering the capped client array. Change the /assets default order at app/api/v3/assets/route.ts:141 to stalest-first or add an explicit "Needs a rescan" filter, and order /shares by share creation. Back all of it with useQueryParam per qolf-10 so a filtered view is linkable. On mobile these do not fit inline, so put them behind one "Filters" trigger opening components/ui/sheet.tsx with the active-filter count on the trigger.

title: A new account meets an eight-step feature-tour modal before it can reach the scan box, and the tour's copy is exactly the generic voice CLAUDE.md bans
description: OnboardingTour is mounted first in the dashboard tree (app/dashboard/page.tsx:876) and opens on any account where onboardingCompleted is false (components/shared/onboarding-tour.tsx:83-92), rendering a full-screen backdrop at :122. STEPS at :24-77 is eight entries. The signup-to-first-scan path is already landing, signup form, verification email, verify page which auto-redirects after a 2 second timer (app/verify-email/VerifyEmailClient.tsx:76-79), and then this modal. The copy is generic in exactly the ways CLAUDE.md and audits/AUDIT-011/design-language.md section F prohibit: "Your all-in-one web vulnerability scanner. Let's walk you through the key features so you can get the most out of VulnRadar" (:28), "Great for verifying that you fixed vulnerabilities" (:46), "You're All Set!" (:71), against a landing page whose voice is "Paste a URL. Get findings, not a grade out of ten." (components/auth/auth-split-layout.tsx:105-107).
impact: The first thing a new user sees inside the product is eight screens of feature marketing about teams, webhooks and CI integration, none of which they can evaluate before running one scan. Skipping is one click, so most users will skip and learn nothing, and the ones who do not spend eight clicks before reaching the box. It is also the first impression that contradicts the landing page's voice, which is the strongest work in the repo.
recommendation: Delete the blocking modal and let the account land on the scan form, which components/scanner/scan-hero.tsx already introduces. Replace it with two cheaper things. First, a single dismissible strip above the form for a brand-new account, in the landing page's voice, along the lines of "Paste any URL. Nothing to install: the request goes out from our servers, not your browser." Second, one-time contextual hints attached to the features they describe and shown after the moment each becomes relevant: a "Compare this against your last run" pointer the second time the same host is scanned, an "API keys and schedules live here" pointer the first time the Developer tab opens. The existing POST /api/v3/auth/onboarding completion flag (:96) and the tour-replay entry at components/profile/tabs/profile-general-tab.tsx:441 can both stay, with the replay opening a static "What's here" page instead of a wizard. The step list at :139-203, which shows the whole shape at once and lets you jump anywhere, is the good part and is worth keeping as that page.

title: Four signed-in pages open with the same four-cell aggregate strip, and on /history three of its four cells are derivable from the other one and from the heading directly above it
description:
The identical container `grid grid-cols-2 sm:grid-cols-4 gap-px bg-border overflow-hidden rounded-md border border-border` opens four pages: /dashboard (components/scanner/dashboard.tsx:148 and :261), /history (components/history/history-stats.tsx:66), /shares (components/shares/shares-stats.tsx:64) and /assets (components/assets/assets-stats.tsx:53). All four hold four cells built from a `Cell` or `StatCell` function with the same body: a StatIcon, a `text-2xl font-semibold tabular-nums` number and an `text-[11px] text-muted-foreground` label. Adjacent pages therefore open with an identical template, which is what CLAUDE.md's layout-patterns-to-avoid list and design-language.md tell-tale 6 call out.

On /history it is also redundant content. The h1 subtitle at app/history/page.tsx:579-585 already reads `{scans.length} scans on record`, and the very next element, HistoryStats at :588, opens with a Total scans cell holding the same `scans.length` (history-stats.tsx:55, :67-72). Of the remaining three cells, Came back clean (:56) and Had findings (:57) are complementary filters of the same array and sum back to the first cell, so three of the four numbers carry no information the reader did not already have. Only Findings total (:58-61) is new.
impact: Every signed-in list page looks like every other signed-in list page above the fold, and the strip costs a screenful before the reader reaches the thing the page is for. On /history specifically the reader is shown the same number twice in adjacent elements.
recommendation:
Keep the strip where it earns its place and vary the others, following the nine-different-layouts principle the landing page demonstrates.

- /history: delete HistoryStats entirely (remove the import and the call at app/history/page.tsx:588, delete components/history/history-stats.tsx and its skeleton branch). Fold the one number worth keeping into the existing subtitle at :579-585: `{n} scans on record, {m} findings across them, kept for {retention}`. That removes a component and a screenful and loses nothing.
- /shares: replace the four cells with the SeverityDistribution bar from components/scanner/severity-badge.tsx:129-190, whose own docblock explains it reads as one bar rather than five cards. Clean, warnings and unsafe are proportions of one whole, which is exactly what that component is for.
- /assets: same substitution, the four cells are Hosts scanned plus a three-way safety split.
- /dashboard: keep the strip. It is the one page where four independent counters are the right shape, and it is already paired with the activity sparkline rather than standing alone.

title: The domain portfolio UI renders at two URLs because the move to /attack-surface never removed the copy in the profile Developer tab
description:
DomainsSection (components/profile/tabs/developer/domains-section.tsx:97, 515 lines) has two importers. app/attack-surface/page.tsx:54 renders it as a top-level page reached from the HistoryViewTabs strip, and that file's own doc comment at :12-14 states the reason: the domain-verification UI already existed but was buried in the profile Developer tab, so this surfaces it as its own tab. components/profile/tabs/profile-developer-tab.tsx still lists it as a fourth sub-tab at :82 and still renders it at :754, reachable at /profile?tab=developer&dtab=domains.

The two surfaces are the same component with different chrome: /attack-surface gives it an h1, an explanatory paragraph about what verifying a domain unlocks, and the History/Assets/Attack Surface/Public Scans tab strip; the profile copy gives it a sub-tab label and nothing else. Verifying a domain from one and then opening the other shows two independently fetched copies of the same list.
impact: Two URLs for one feature, so a user who bookmarks or is linked to one never discovers the other, and the profile copy is the worse of the two because it has none of the explanatory framing that tells the user what domain verification is for. It also doubles the maintenance surface: any change to the surrounding affordances has to be made twice or the two drift.
recommendation: Finish the move. Delete the `{ id: "domains", label: "Domains", icon: ShieldCheck }` entry from DEVELOPER_SECTIONS at components/profile/tabs/profile-developer-tab.tsx:82 and the `{activeSection === "domains" && ...}` branch at :754, and drop domains from the DeveloperSection type. In its place put a one-line pointer in the Developer tab's header, `Verified domains moved to Attack surface`, linking to ROUTES.ATTACK_SURFACE, so anyone with the old deep link lands somewhere useful. Add a redirect from ?tab=developer&dtab=domains to /attack-surface in the dtab handling at app/profile/page.tsx:110-120 for the same reason.

title: Scheduled scans and webhooks sit three levels deep under Account Settings while Badge, a one-time embed snippet, is a top-level nav item
description:
The signed-in nav (components/scanner/header.tsx:26-33) has eight entries: Scanner, History, Repos, Compare, Shared, Teams, Badge, Profile. Badge is /badge, a page that generates an embeddable status badge snippet, which a user configures once and never returns to. It sits at the same level as History.

Scheduled Scans, the product's recurring-monitoring feature with its own documentation section at app/docs/scheduled-scans, is at /profile?tab=developer&dtab=schedules: Profile in the nav, then the Developer tab (app/profile/page.tsx:645-651), then the Scheduled Scans sub-tab (profile-developer-tab.tsx:81). Three levels, and the page it lives on is titled Account Settings (app/profile/page.tsx:679). Webhooks are in the same place (:80). Both are things a user returns to, filed under settings; the header's DEVELOPER_HREF constant at header.tsx:23 already acknowledges the depth problem by hard-coding a shortcut to the Developer tab, but that shortcut is not a nav item.

Meanwhile Assets, Attack Surface and Public Scans are sub-tabs of History via HistoryViewTabs (components/history/history-view-tabs.tsx:8-13), which is a sensible grouping and shows the pattern already exists.
impact: The two features that create recurring engagement, scheduled scans and webhooks, are the hardest to find, and the one that creates none is the most prominent. A user setting up monitoring has to guess that a scheduling feature lives behind a tab called Developer inside a page called Account Settings.
recommendation: Rebalance without adding nav width. Replace the Badge entry at components/scanner/header.tsx:32 with a Monitoring entry pointing at a new /monitoring route, and give that route the same HistoryViewTabs-style sub-strip holding Scheduled Scans, Webhooks and Alerts. Move SchedulesSection and WebhooksSection there by import, exactly as app/attack-surface/page.tsx:54 already does for DomainsSection, and remove their sub-tab entries from DEVELOPER_SECTIONS (profile-developer-tab.tsx:80-81) so the Developer tab is left with API Keys alone, at which point rename that tab to API. Move Badge to the profile Social tab, next to the other share and embed affordances, which is where a one-time embed snippet belongs.

title: Nothing replaces the removed timer: the status endpoint returns progress but no findings, so the wait has no payoff until it ends
category: scanning page: replacement for the timer
description:
This is the replacement proposal AUDIT-011#scan-05 asked for and did not specify. It is scoped strictly to what the API produces today, verified by reading the endpoint and the producer.

WHAT EXISTS NOW. GET /api/v3/scan/status/[id] builds `responseBody` at app/api/v3/scan/status/[id]/route.ts:162-168 with exactly five keys while a scan is live: `status`, `currentCategory`, `categoriesCompleted`, `categoriesTotal`, `elapsedMs`. On `completed` it adds the whole `result`; on `failed` it adds `error`. The client reads three of them (app/dashboard/page.tsx:146-150) and drops `elapsedMs` on the floor. The producer is `createProgressTracker` in lib/scanner/scan-jobs.ts:117-139, whose hook fires once per CATEGORY as `start` and once as `done`, writing `current_category` / `categories_completed` / `categories_total` to scan_history. The hook's type is `(category: string, phase) => void` (lib/scanner/types.ts:352-355): it carries no check count and no findings.

So of the three things the brief asked for, the API supports exactly one and a half today:
1. "Which check category is running" -- SUPPORTED. `currentCategory` is a real Category id, and lib/scanner/category-meta.ts already holds a client-safe label and one-line blurb for all 18, importing only a type.
2. "How many of the ~797 checks are done" -- NOT SUPPORTED as checks; supported as families. `categoriesCompleted / categoriesTotal` is real and exact (route.ts:332-339 derives the denominator from `getPlannedSyncCategories` plus `getPlannedAsyncBranches`, never estimated). Per-check counts are computed but only at the end: lib/scanner/engine.ts:206-211 returns `checksRun` and `checksSkipped` after the whole loop, and they reach the user only as the "Checks run" stat on the finished view (components/scanner/scan-summary.tsx:295-302).
3. "Findings streaming in as discovered" -- NOT SUPPORTED AT ALL. `runSyncChecks` accumulates into a local `findings` array (engine.ts:156) and nothing reads it until `dedupeFindings` at :205. scan_history.findings is written once, by `finalizeScanSuccess` (scan-jobs.ts:240-245), in the same UPDATE that flips status to `completed`. There is no partial-findings column and no partial-findings field on the poll response.
impact: After scanui-01 the card would show a family name, a bar, and nothing else, which is less information than the clock it replaced. The scan is the product's whole value proposition and for its entire duration the user is shown zero of its output, then all of it at once, then (until AUDIT-011#scan-08 is fixed) a blur over the top of it. The visible work is a large part of a scanner's perceived worth and this page currently spends the wait proving nothing.
recommendation:
Build it in three tiers, each independently shippable.

TIER 1, zero backend change, ship with scanui-01. Three real numbers in a mono definition list, all already on the wire:
  FAMILIES  12 / 18      (categoriesCompleted / categoriesTotal)
  RUNNING   DNS          (CATEGORY_META[currentCategory].label)
  NEXT      Email        (the next entry in the client's own planned family list)
plus the one-line `FAMILY_STEP` sentence for the running family, which is already written and is good copy ("Grepping responses for keys and tokens"). Keep those strings; they are the best thing in the current component.

TIER 2, one generated file, still no server change, gives a real check count. scripts/compile-checks-knowledge.mjs already iterates lib/scanner/checks-data/<category>.json per category (see its loop and the write at :283-286) and emits lib/config/check-stats.generated.ts, which is client-safe (`EXACT_CHECK_COUNT = 797`, `EXACT_CHECK_CATEGORY_COUNT = 18`, no runtime imports). Add one export: `export const EXACT_CHECKS_BY_CATEGORY: Record<string, number> = {...}`. The client then sums the counts of the families already marked done and renders `CHECKS 531 / 797` in `font-mono tabular-nums`, rising in real steps. Label it honestly: this counts the checks in the families that have reported, so it will slightly overstate against the final `checksRun` (page checks whose `requirementsMet` gate fails are counted as skipped at engine.ts:186-188). Either accept a final reconciliation to the real `checksRun`, or emit legacy-only counts and label the row `RULES`.

TIER 3, the real prize, and it needs a backend change. Stream findings as they are discovered:
  a) Widen `ScanProgressHook` (lib/scanner/types.ts:352-355) to `(category, phase, snapshot?: { found: number; newFindings: { severity: Severity; title: string }[] })`.
  b) In lib/scanner/engine.ts, at the `onProgress?.(category, "done")` call at :203, pass the findings pushed during that category's iteration (the loop already has them; slice `findings` from the index recorded before `onProgress?.(category, "start")` at :166).
  c) In `createProgressTracker` (lib/scanner/scan-jobs.ts:117-139) append those into a new `scan_history.partial_findings JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]'` column in the same fire-and-forget UPDATE that already runs there, keeping the existing `WHERE status IN ('pending','running')` guard so a late write after completion is a no-op. Add the column in instrumentation.ts beside the other scan_history additions, and to scripts/migrate (see AUDIT-013#migrate-01: this is exactly the kind of column that gets missed).
  d) In app/api/v3/scan/status/[id]/route.ts add `responseBody.partialFindings = row.partial_findings` in the live branch only (never in the `completed` branch, where `result.findings` is authoritative). Cap it server-side at ~40 entries and store only `{severity, title}`, never evidence or remediation, so a 2-second poll stays small.
  e) On completion, clear `partial_findings` in `finalizeScanSuccess`'s UPDATE so a re-poll of a finished scan does not carry two lists.
The one honesty trap: `dedupeFindings` (engine.ts:205) runs after the last category, so a streamed count can go DOWN at the end. Present the live list under the label "Found so far" and let the completed view's real summary replace it wholesale, rather than animating a number downward.

What NOT to do: do not synthesise a percentage from `elapsedMs`, and do not use `elapsedMs` at all on this screen. It is the same number scanui-01 removes, just served from the server.

title: The scanning card is a boxed progress bar over a two-column grid of 20 identical status rows, which is the templated pattern the design language names, and its labels clip on a phone
description:
Measured against audits/AUDIT-011/design-language.md and its 14-point checklist. The scanning state is app/dashboard/page.tsx:910-922, a single centred `<div className="flex justify-center pt-10 sm:pt-16">` wrapping components/scanner/scanning-indicator.tsx.

DEVIATIONS, each verified at a line:

1. Tell-tale 5 and E1. scanning-indicator.tsx:307-344 is a `grid grid-cols-1 ... sm:grid-cols-2` of up to 20 rows, every row structurally identical: a 14px `rounded-full` glyph followed by a truncated label. That is the named anti-pattern in list form. The design language's alternatives for exactly this job are the divided list (`divide-y divide-border/50`), the mono-term `<dl>`, and the real table (D4). Four of the nine landing sections use no card grid at all.

2. Tell-tale 4, accent restraint. The doctrine is at most two accented elements per section, documented twice in code comments (landing-categories.tsx:6-11, landing-open-source.tsx:18-19). This card has: the mode pill (:262, `border-primary/20 bg-primary/10 text-primary`), the bar fill (:300, `bg-primary`), and one primary-tinted circle per completed row (:321, `border-primary/40 bg-primary/15 text-primary`) plus the running one (:322, `border-primary bg-primary`). By the last second of a full scan that is roughly 22 primary-tinted elements in one card.

3. Tell-tale 1 and C1. Section rhythm is `py-16 sm:py-20`. The scanning state uses `pt-10 sm:pt-16` with no bottom padding of its own (app/dashboard/page.tsx:911), a third value.

4. C5 radius ladder. `:259` is `rounded-md`, which resolves to `calc(var(--radius) - 2px)` via tailwind.config.mjs:75-79 and is the BUTTON radius. The spec's content card is `rounded-xl`. components/scanner/scan-form.tsx:562 and components/scanner/dashboard-error-state.tsx:182 make the same choice, so all three surfaces of this page are consistent with each other and none matches the spec.

5. C1 divider opacity. "`border-border/50` is the divider, not `border-border`. Full opacity is reserved for the footer's outer edge and card outlines." The internal dividers here are `border-b border-border` (:261) and `border-t border-border` (:307), both full opacity. The house content card (D1) uses `border-b border-border/60` internally.

6. D3 pill idiom. `:262` is `rounded border ... px-2 py-0.5 text-xs font-medium`. The house pill is `rounded-full`, `text-[10px]`, mono or `uppercase tracking-wider`, border at /25 to /30. The severity badge is the one deliberate `rounded` exception and this is not it, so it is a third pill grammar.

7. B2 type scale, and it is also an a11y defect (filed separately as scanui-08): the card has no heading of any kind. `ScanHero` (the page's only `<h1>`) lives inside the `status === "idle"` branch at app/dashboard/page.tsx:887 and is unmounted the instant scanning starts.

8. MOBILE, the one measurable usability defect here. The row label at :331-338 is `min-w-0 truncate` inside a `grid-cols-1` column below the `sm` breakpoint, so it clips on one line with no wrap, no `title` attribute and no tooltip. The strings it clips are the longest ones in FAMILY_STEP: "Parsing page content for mixed content and inline script" (55 chars), "Probing forms & endpoints for XSS, SQLi, SSTI & more" (51), "Looking for leaked paths, versions and stack traces" (50). Derived from the class list rather than measured in a browser: at a 375px viewport the available text width is roughly 375 minus 32 (main `px-4`) minus 32 (card `px-4`) minus about 22 (glyph plus `gap-2`), so about 289px, against roughly 300 to 310px needed for 55 characters at `text-xs`. At 640px and up the same strings sit in a half-width column and clip harder. Also, at one column the list is 20 rows tall, so on a 667px phone the card runs past the fold for a state that lasts a few seconds.

9. Tell-tale 14, motion. globals.css:141-151 collapses CSS `animation-duration` and `transition-duration` under `prefers-reduced-motion`, so the bar's `transition-[width] duration-500` (:300) is covered. The `requestAnimationFrame` settle ramp at :227-248 is not: it writes `style={{ width }}` from JS over SETTLE_ANIMATION_MS and ignores the media query entirely.

10. Structural. The three states are three mutually exclusive full-page branches (app/dashboard/page.tsx:885-958). Submitting the form unmounts ScanHero, ScanForm and the whole Dashboard widget block and replaces them with one small centred card; completion unmounts that card and mounts DashboardResults. Nothing is shared between them, so the page's contents are wholly swapped twice per scan.
impact: This is the highest-traffic transient surface in the product: every scan passes through it, and it is the surface the section brief singles out as reading AI-generated. The mobile clipping is a real loss of information, not a matter of taste: on a phone the user cannot read what is currently running. The three-way content swap means the page never feels like one thing filling in, which is what a scanner should feel like.
recommendation:
Rebuild as one surface that transforms in place. Concretely, so a developer can build it without re-deciding anything. STRUCTURE. Keep the page container `w-full max-w-6xl mx-auto px-4 sm:px-6` (already `CONTAINER` at app/dashboard/page.tsx:61). Replace the `flex justify-center pt-10 sm:pt-16` wrapper with `py-16 sm:py-20` (C1 standard rhythm) and do not centre: left-align, like every other app surface. HEADING BLOCK, mirroring ScanHero's geometry so the swap from idle is a text change, not a layout change:

797 checks across 18 families. Findings appear here as each family reports, before the run finishes.

Pull 797 and 18 from lib/config/check-stats.generated.ts (`EXACT_CHECK_COUNT`, `EXACT_CHECK_CATEGORY_COUNT`), never hardcoded (tell-tale 8). BODY, 2-column asymmetric split (E2 idiom, mirrors the hero): `grid gap-8 lg:grid-cols-[minmax(0,1fr)_minmax(0,1.15fr)] lg:gap-12`. LEFT: the run readout, in the ResponseReadout grammar (components/shared/response-readout.tsx:161-216), which is the house signature and already renders "the literal shape of scanning". `overflow-hidden rounded-xl border border-border bg-card font-mono`. - Header, `flex items-baseline gap-2 border-b border-border/60 bg-muted/20 px-5 py-3`: `GET` in `shrink-0 font-semibold text-primary`, then `min-w-0 flex-1 truncate text-foreground` hostname, then the mode label as plain `text-xs text-muted-foreground` (drop the pill entirely; it is the least important thing on screen and it is costing an accent). - Body, `px-5 py-4`: one line of `text-sm text-foreground` carrying the current family's FAMILY_STEP sentence (keep those strings verbatim, they are the best copy in the file), then the bar, then a mono-term `
` (D4 pattern 2): `
` with rows FAMILIES `12 / 18`, CHECKS `531 / 797`, FOUND `7`, values in `font-mono tabular-nums text-foreground`. - Bar: `h-1.5 w-full overflow-hidden rounded-full bg-muted` with a `bg-primary transition-[width] duration-300 ease-out` fill. Reuse the geometry of `SeverityDistribution` (components/scanner/severity-badge.tsx:129-190), which is already the canonical "one bar, not five cards" aggregate. - Family list, replacing the 20-cell grid: a `divide-y divide-border/50` list, each row `flex items-baseline justify-between gap-3 py-2`. Left is `CATEGORY_META[c].label` (lib/scanner/category-meta.ts, client-safe, 14 chars at most: "Info disclosure"), right is `font-mono text-xs tabular-nums` check count for that family. State encoded by weight, not by 20 tinted circles: pending `text-muted-foreground/50`, done `text-muted-foreground` with the count in `text-foreground`, running `text-foreground font-medium` on a row carrying `border-l-2 border-primary pl-3`. That single rail is the only accent in the list, which brings the card to three accented elements total (the `GET` word, the bar fill, the one rail). - Footer, `flex items-center justify-between gap-3 border-t border-border/60 bg-muted/20 px-5 py-2.5 text-xs`: cancel on the left as `

title: A shared scan report has no per-report metadata or image: every share link is titled "Shared Scan Report", described with the site-wide app description, and carries the generic marketing OG card
description: app/shared/[token]/layout.tsx:7 is the only metadata source for the route and it calls privatePageMetadata("Shared Scan Report", "/shared"). lib/seo/metadata.ts:130 expands that to pageMetadata with description = APP_DESCRIPTION (the generic site description), image = SEO_OG_IMAGE ("/og-image.png", the static marketing card), and canonical/og:url = APP_URL + "/shared", a path that has no route at all (there is no app/shared/page.tsx). app/host/[hostname]/layout.tsx:8 does the same with "Host Report" and "/host". Nothing per-report reaches the head. There is no opengraph-image.tsx anywhere in the repo and no use of next/og or ImageResponse (grepped across app/, components/, lib/, scripts/): zero dynamic social images exist. The data needed is already available server side by token: app/api/v3/shared/[token]/route.ts:30 selects sh.url, sh.summary, sh.findings_count and sh.scanned_at from scan_history by SHA-256 token hash, with the expiry and revocation gates already written. The page itself cannot supply it (app/shared/[token]/page.tsx:1 is "use client" and fetches in useEffect), but the layout is a server component and can export generateMetadata({ params }). The rendering toolchain also already exists: public/og-image.svg is a 1200x630 template whose right-hand card is literally a mock scan result ("your-domain.com / RISK SCORE 2 of 10 / TOP FINDINGS"), and scripts/build-og-image.mjs rasterizes it with sharp.
impact: The strongest visual asset the project owns (AUDIT-011 names the OG image one of its three best artifacts) is spent showing a fake domain and fake findings, while the real ones are one query away. A share of a genuine report previews identically to a share of the homepage, so nothing in the unfurl tells a reader that someone scanned a specific site and found specific problems. That is the entire viral mechanic of this product category, unused. Note the privacy math is favourable: whoever the unfurler is already holds the token, which grants the full report, so putting the hostname and severity counts in the head leaks nothing the link does not already grant.
recommendation: Add `export async function generateMetadata({ params })` to app/shared/[token]/layout.tsx that hashes the token the same way app/api/v3/shared/[token]/route.ts:24 does, selects url, summary and scanned_at, and returns pageMetadata({ noIndex: true, title: `Security scan of ${hostname}`, description: `${critical} critical, ${high} high and ${medium} medium findings on ${hostname}, scanned ${date} by VulnRadar. Open the full report.`, image: `/shared/${token}/opengraph-image` }). Fall back to the current generic strings when the token misses, is expired, or is revoked, so an invalid link leaks nothing. Then add app/shared/[token]/opengraph-image.tsx using ImageResponse from next/og (bundled with next 15.5.23, no new dependency) at size 1200x630, laid out as the right-hand card of public/og-image.svg: hostname, risk score out of 10, and the top five finding titles with severity dots in the --severity-* colours. Do the same for app/host/[hostname]/. twitter.card is already "summary_large_image" via lib/seo/metadata.ts:116, so nothing else changes.

title: The security badge is the product's only backlink loop and every badge points at a /shared/ URL that is Disallowed in robots.txt and served noindex, nofollow, so the inbound links are thrown away
description: app/docs/sharing/page.tsx:386 publishes the embed snippet users paste onto their own sites: ``. Both halves of that snippet point at paths that robots.txt forbids: `/shared/` via lib/seo/routes.ts:121 and `/api/` via line 108, both spread into the wildcard Disallow at app/robots.ts:60. On top of that the link target itself serves `noindex, nofollow` (app/shared/[token]/layout.tsx:7 via privatePageMetadata, lib/seo/metadata.ts:85). So the destination cannot be crawled, cannot be indexed, and carries nofollow. The image is an SVG served from /api/v3/badge/[token] (app/api/v3/badge/[token]/route.ts:122, Content-Type image/svg+xml), which is also Disallowed and which social and image crawlers do not render.
impact: A security badge on a customer's site is the standard organic-growth loop for this product category: it is how Security Headers, SSL Labs and Mozilla Observatory accumulate their link graph. Here the feature is built, documented, and produces a link that search engines are explicitly told to ignore. Every customer who installs a badge gives the product a link worth nothing.
recommendation: Point the documented `<a href>` at `/host/<hostname>` instead of `/shared/<token>`: it is the stable, per-host public page for the same site (app/api/v3/host/[hostname]/route.ts only ever serves public scans, and its host_reputation row is deleted when a scan is made private), it does not expose a token in someone else's page source, and it is the page a stranger arriving from the badge actually wants. Then do seo-09 so that target is indexable and followable. Update the snippet at app/docs/sharing/page.tsx:386 and anywhere the badge UI generates the same HTML. Keep the SVG badge image where it is; the link, not the image, is what carries the value.

title: /host/[hostname] is kept noindex and robots-Disallowed on the stated grounds that the URL space is "not enumerable", which is false: host_reputation is a table and /public-scans already paginates it
description: lib/seo/routes.ts:100-106 justifies excluding /host/ and /shared/ together: "Tokenised or per-entity URLs (/shared/<token>, /browser/<id>, /host/<hostname>). Not enumerable ahead of time, so there is no fixed list to publish a sitemap entry or canonical for." That reasoning is correct for /shared/<token> and /browser/<id>, which are secrets. It is not correct for /host/<hostname>: app/api/v3/host/[hostname]/route.ts:99 reads from the `host_reputation` table keyed on `host`, so the full list is a single SELECT, and app/public-scans/page.tsx already renders a paginated, sitemapped, indexable directory of exactly this data. The data is public by construction, not by accident: app/api/v3/host/[hostname]/route.ts:140 gates the live findings on `is_public = true`, and the route's own comment states the host_reputation row is deleted when its source scan is made private. The page also already has a per-host trend chart (components/host/danger-score-trend.tsx). Today the page ships privatePageMetadata("Host Report", "/host") (app/host/[hostname]/layout.tsx:8), so it has no per-host title, no per-host description, a canonical pointing at /host which is not a route, and noindex.
impact: "<domain> security report" and "is <domain> safe" are the highest-volume query shapes in this product category, and they are the entire organic strategy of Security Headers, SSL Labs, Mozilla Observatory and urlscan.io. The product already generates the pages that answer them, already restricts them to public data, already links them from an indexable directory, and then blocks all of them. The 749 /checks pages target "how to fix X" intent, which converts worse: someone searching a check name is fixing a problem they already found, while someone searching a domain is looking for a scanner.
recommendation: Three changes. (1) Replace app/host/[hostname]/layout.tsx with an async generateMetadata({ params }) that resolves the host via the same host_reputation lookup and returns pageMetadata({ title: `${host} security report`, description: `${host} scored ${dangerScore}/10 on ${date}: ${critical} critical and ${high} high findings across headers, TLS, cookies and DNS.`, path: `/host/${host}`, noIndex: !known || findings.length === 0 }), so an unscanned or empty host stays noindex and only real reports are indexable. (2) Remove "/host/" from DISALLOWED_PATHS in lib/seo/routes.ts:122, leaving "/shared/" and "/browser/" in place. (3) Publish the URLs: add a second sitemap (Next 15 supports generateSitemaps(), or a plain app/sitemap-hosts.xml/route.ts) that selects host and last_scanned_at from host_reputation and emits a real per-host lastmod, and reference both from a sitemap index. Note app/sitemap.ts is currently `force-static` so the host sitemap must be a separate dynamic route. Pair with seo-02 so each host page also gets a real social card, and with seo-08 so badges point here.

title: The 749 check pages call generateStaticParams and produce zero prerendered HTML, so the entire organic surface is an uncacheable per-request render and Cloudflare returns a MISS on 100 percent of crawler traffic
description: This is the SEO quantification of AUDIT-012#fe-01 and AUDIT-012#perf-17 (root cause: app/layout.tsx:146 awaits headers() for the CSP nonce, which opts every segment beneath it into per-request dynamic rendering). Do not re-file the root cause. What matters for section 19 is the shape of the loss. app/checks/[id]/page.tsx:34 exports generateStaticParams() returning all 749 check ids, and the file's own comment at lines 29-31 states it produces nothing: "The root layout reads headers() for its CSP nonce, so the whole app already renders per-request." app/checks/category/[category]/page.tsx:27 and app/alternatives/[competitor]/page.tsx:17 do the same. AUDIT-012#fe-01 measured the committed build: .next/prerender-manifest.json lists exactly 5 prerendered routes (robots.txt, sitemap.xml, manifest.webmanifest, llms.txt, llms-full.txt) against 311 app-build-manifest entries, and Next sets `cache-control: private, no-cache, no-store, max-age=0, must-revalidate` on dynamically rendered app pages. The sitemap I computed from lib/seo/routes.ts contains 805 URLs: 33 hand-listed, 18 categories, 5 alternatives, 749 checks. Every one is an origin React render with an uncacheable response, on the same single Node process that runs scans. No route sets `revalidate`, so there is no ISR fallback either. On top of that, AUDIT-012#fe-02 measured that the root-layout ChatWidget puts react-markdown plus remark-gfm (144 KB raw / 44 KB gzipped) and an /api/v3/ai/info request on all 311 routes, and AUDIT-011#docs-05 measured /checks at ~190 KB of HTML for 754 list items.
impact: Crawl budget is spent on origin CPU rather than edge bytes: a full Googlebot pass over the sitemap is 805 cold server-side renders, each also serving a JS bundle Googlebot must parse in its rendering pass, with a Cache-Control header that forbids both the CDN and Googlebot's own cache from reusing anything on the next crawl. Nothing in this repo can be measured for TTFB here (no build, no deploy, no Docker on this machine), but the mechanism is unambiguous: the HTML cache hit rate on the organic surface is structurally zero, and content that is byte-identical between deploys is regenerated for every crawler hit and every visitor. Crawler traffic also directly competes with scan execution for the same CPU, so an organic traffic spike degrades the product.
recommendation: Separate the SEO surface from the nonce. Move the public content routes (/checks, /checks/category, /alternatives, /tools, /docs, /legal, /landing, /pricing) into a route group such as app/(marketing)/ with its own layout.tsx that does NOT call headers(), and lift the inline auth-cache script out of the root layout for that group (it is only useful to signed-in users, who are not on these pages). Those routes then prerender from their existing generateStaticParams and become CDN-cacheable. Because the inline script's content is deterministic (it is built from STAFF_ROLES at build time), the alternative fix is a hash-based CSP for that one script, which lets the root layout drop headers() entirely. Either way, add `export const revalidate = 86400` to the check and category routes so a content edit still reaches the edge without a deploy. Verify by checking that .next/prerender-manifest.json lists the 749 check routes after the change.

title: A failed team-members fetch renders "Members 0" over a blank list, "0 members, Your role: " with the role blank, and silently strips every management control from the owner
description: app/teams/page.tsx:280-293 (`refreshMembers`) fetches GET /api/v3/teams/members and only acts inside `if (res.ok)`. On a non-ok response or a thrown request, `members`, `invites` and `currentRole` all keep their prior values (on first open: `[]`, `[]` and `""` from :59), `membersLoading` goes false in the finally at :291, and no error is recorded anywhere. components/teams/team-members-list.tsx then renders the loaded branch: :58-63 prints the header "Members" with the count `members.length`, which is 0, and :182-190 falls to a `divide-y` container with nothing in it, because there is no empty branch at all. The role explainer at :181 is gated on `members.length > 0` so it vanishes too. Separately, `currentRole` staying "" makes `hasTeamPermission("", ...)` false everywhere, so components/teams/team-detail-header.tsx:59-60 hides the rename control and the Invite button, and :132 renders `Your role: ` with an empty span. A team always contains at least its owner, so `members.length === 0` is not a state the data can produce: it is reachable only through a failed fetch, which means the blank card is always a lie.
impact: A team owner opening their own team during a backend blip is told the team has zero members, sees their own role as blank, and finds the Invite and Rename controls gone. The natural reading is that they were removed from their own team or that their permissions were revoked. There is no retry, no message, and nothing distinguishes it from a real permission change. The identical shape applies to `handleViewMemberScans` at :459-479, where a failed fetch renders a member's scan list as empty, which in a compliance context reads as "this person has run no scans".
recommendation: In app/teams/page.tsx:280-293 add an else branch setting the existing `actionError` state, which already has a rendered destructive band at :515-525, with "Couldn't load this team's members. Nothing has changed, try again." and keep the previous members array rather than showing zero. In components/teams/team-members-list.tsx add an explicit branch for `!loading && members.length === 0` that renders an error block rather than a blank div, since that state is unreachable from real data. Do not set `currentRole` from a failed response; leave the header's role chip and its permission-gated controls in a pending state instead of silently resolving to viewer-level.

title: Coverage measures only .ts, so 419 React files and 95,294 lines are invisible, and with environment:node and no jsdom the suite cannot render a component even if someone wrote a test
category: whole layer outside the test harness
description: coverage.include is ["lib/**/*.ts", "app/**/*.ts"] (vitest.config.ts:31). The glob `*.ts` does not match `.tsx`. The coverage run confirms it: exactly 412 files are measured, which is 250 lib/*.ts plus 162 app/*.ts, and not one .tsx. Unmeasured: 266 components/*.tsx plus 47 components/*.ts (313 files, 65,147 lines), 152 app/*.tsx (30,147 lines), and 1 lib/*.tsx. Separately, test.environment is "node" (line 23) and package.json lists no jsdom, no happy-dom, and no @testing-library/* in either dependencies or devDependencies, so no test can mount a React tree at all. The eight files under tests/components/ cover 8 of 313 component files (2.6%), and six of those eight targets are plain .ts utility modules (queue-status-utils.ts, settings-registry-utils.ts, use-unsaved-changes-warning.ts, admin/utils.ts, schedule-time-utils.ts, ai-review-gate.ts); only danger-score-trend.tsx and auth-provider.tsx are .tsx, and those tests can reach only their non-rendering exports.
impact: Every form-validation rule, every conditional that hides a paid feature behind a plan check, every auth-state branch in a client component, and every result renderer is untested and unmeasured. A regression that shows a Pro-only control to a free user, or that renders a scan as clean when findings exist, reaches production with a green CI. The measurement gap makes it worse than it looks: the 81.02% headline reads as broad health while a third of the app's lines are simply not in the denominator.
recommendation: Two steps, and the first is cheap. Change coverage.include to ["lib/**/*.{ts,tsx}", "app/**/*.{ts,tsx}", "components/**/*.{ts,tsx}", "middleware.ts"] so the real denominator is visible even before any test is written; expect the headline to drop, which is the accurate number. Then add jsdom plus @testing-library/react as devDependencies and an environmentMatchGlobs entry mapping tests/components/** to jsdom, and start with the highest-risk components: components/scanner/scan-form.tsx, the plan-gated controls, and the shared ScanResultDetail renderer.

title: middleware.ts, the 546-line request gate for every route in the app, sits outside coverage.include so its 365-line test suite produces no measurable coverage
description: middleware.ts is 546 lines and lives at the repo root, so it matches neither "lib/**/*.ts" nor "app/**/*.ts" in coverage.include (vitest.config.ts:31). It does not appear in the coverage-summary.json I generated: filtering the 412 measured files for 'middleware' returns nothing. tests/middleware.test.ts exists and is 365 lines, so the file is not untested, but there is no way to tell which of its branches the suite reaches. This matters because middleware is where the public-path allowlist and the auth redirect live, and AUDIT-012 filed three separate HIGH findings against that allowlist (authz-01, authz-02, authz-03: the public host report API, all three staff-oidc endpoints, and the public contact form all missing from PUBLIC_PATHS, each breaking the feature for logged-out visitors). lib/config/public-paths.ts reports 100% statements but only 1 statement, because it is a data table: line coverage says nothing about whether the table is correct. instrumentation.ts is excluded outright (vitest.config.ts:38) and is 3,639 lines holding 72 CREATE TABLE and 97 CREATE INDEX statements.
impact: The single file that decides whether a request is authenticated, redirected, or allowed through unauthenticated has an unknown tested fraction. A branch added to it, for example a new public path or a new bypass condition, is invisible to both the coverage report and to a reviewer asking 'is this covered?'. The AUDIT-012 authz findings show the concrete cost: three features silently broken for every logged-out visitor and crawler, shipped past a green suite.
recommendation: Add "middleware.ts" to coverage.include in vitest.config.ts so the file is measured, then read the resulting branch percentage and fill the gaps in tests/middleware.test.ts. Separately, add a table-driven test that walks every entry in PUBLIC_PATHS and asserts each named route file actually exists, and walks every route.ts the app serves unauthenticated and asserts it is listed, which is the drift the three AUDIT-012 authz findings all were.

title: The two Stripe events that reverse money, charge.refunded and charge.dispute.created, are the only two of nine handled event types with no test
description: app/api/v3/webhooks/stripe/route.ts measures 68.18% statements and 58.3% branches over 264 statements. The handler switch has nine cases: checkout.session.completed (183), customer.subscription.created (296), updated (475), deleted (626), invoice.payment_succeeded (686), invoice.payment_failed (770), payment_intent.succeeded (803), charge.refunded (940), charge.dispute.created (982). Extracting the event-type string literals from tests/app/api/v3/webhooks/stripe/route.test.ts yields eight, and the two missing are charge.refunded and charge.dispute.created. Those two branches each call reverseAiCreditPurchase, reverseGithubCreditPurchase, and reverseBrowserbaseCreditPurchase in a Promise.all (lines 958-962 and 997-1001). The reversal functions themselves are well covered (lib/billing/ai-usage.ts 98.27%, browserbase-usage.ts 100%, github-review-usage.ts 98.59%), so what is untested is the wiring: the partial-refund early-break at line 947, the payment_intent extraction that must handle both a string and an expanded object (lines 953-956 and 989-992), and the dispatch itself. lib/billing/stripe-webhook-setup.ts:29-30 does register both events with Stripe, and tests/lib/billing/stripe-webhook-setup.test.ts covers REQUIRED_EVENTS, but nothing asserts the REQUIRED_EVENTS list and the switch labels agree.
impact: If either case label is renamed, or the payment_intent extraction breaks when Stripe sends an expanded object rather than a string, a refunded or charged-back customer keeps every AI token, GitHub review token, and Browserbase second they paid for. That is direct revenue loss on the exact transactions where the money has already left, and it is silent: the webhook still returns 200, the reversal functions still pass their own unit tests, and the only evidence is a console.log that never fires.
recommendation: Add two describes to tests/app/api/v3/webhooks/stripe/route.test.ts. For charge.refunded assert: refunded:false logs and reverses nothing; refunded:true with a string payment_intent calls all three reverse functions with that id; refunded:true with an expanded payment_intent object extracts .id. For charge.dispute.created assert the same extraction and the three reverse calls. Add one drift test asserting the set of `case` labels in the route equals REQUIRED_EVENTS in lib/billing/stripe-webhook-setup.ts, so registering an event without handling it (or vice versa) fails.

title: The Browserbase client is at 16.87% and page-screenshot at 7.44%, leaving the session-teardown call that stops a paid third-party meter untested at all three of its call sites
description: lib/browserbase/client.ts is the largest sub-50% file in the tree: 243 statements at 16.87% statements / 27.05%-adjacent branches, 662 lines, ten exports (createBrowserSession:112, getBrowserSession:165, getBrowserLiveUrls:189, endBrowserSession:213, pickLiveViewerUrl:273, isBrowserBaseConfigured:279, navigateBrowserSession:298, openCdpPageSession:416, getBrowserSessionLogs:573, parseNetworkRequests:594). tests/lib/browserbase/ contains one file, concurrency-queue.test.ts, which tests a different module. lib/browserbase/network-capture.ts is at 27.05% and lib/scanner/page-screenshot.ts at 7.44% (94 statements, 21.42% functions). endBrowserSession has three call sites that must run or the session keeps billing: app/api/v3/browser/sessions/route.ts:199 (the create-failed cleanup) and :325 (explicit delete), lib/scanner/auth/browser-login.ts:560, and lib/scanner/page-screenshot.ts:267. None of those teardown paths is exercised.
impact: Browserbase is a real paid third party billed by session-seconds, and the credit ledger charges the user for it. A regression where the teardown is skipped on an error path (the exact shape of the route.ts:199 cleanup) leaks a live session per failed scan. Nothing in the product notices: the scan reports a normal failure, the user is charged whatever the ledger recorded, and the overage shows up on the operator's Browserbase invoice at the end of the month. sessions/route.ts:199 already writes `.catch(() => {})`, so even a thrown teardown error is swallowed.
recommendation: Add tests/lib/browserbase/client.test.ts mocking the Browserbase HTTP boundary and assert createBrowserSession sends keepAlive:true, endBrowserSession issues the delete for the right id, and openCdpPageSession honours its timeout argument. Then add teardown assertions at the three call sites: in tests/app/api/v3/browser/sessions/route.test.ts assert endBrowserSession is called when the post-create work throws, and add a page-screenshot test asserting endBrowserSession runs in the failure path as well as the success path.

title: The browser extension is 7,048 lines across 25 TypeScript files with zero tests, no test script, and a CI job that only typechecks, formats, and builds it
category: shipped product with no test suite
description: extension/src/ holds 25 .ts files totalling 7,048 lines. `git ls-files 'extension/**'` matches zero files named *.test.* or *.spec.*, and extension/package.json declares no "test" script: its scripts are dev, build, build:chrome, build:firefox, icons, package, package:source, clean, typecheck, format, format:check. The CI extension job (.github/workflows/ci.yml) runs npm ci, typecheck, format:check, and build for Chrome and Firefox, and nothing else. The untested surface includes the pieces that make security decisions: lib/auth.ts (74 lines, API-key handling), lib/api.ts (259 lines, the calls to the VulnRadar API), lib/storage.ts (249), lib/scan-target.ts (62), lib/url-patterns.ts (108), plus popup/popup.ts at 1,116 lines and background/service-worker.ts. lib/scanner/scan-target-classify.ts in the main app carries an explicit comment that 'the browser extension keeps its own small copy of classifyScanTarget (it's a separate build)', so there is a deliberate duplicate of classification logic on both sides with a test on neither (the app-side copy measures 37.14% statements / 16% branches).
impact: The extension is a published Chrome and Firefox Web Store product with a review and rollback cycle measured in days, so a regression is far more expensive to correct than a web deploy. A typecheck-and-build gate cannot catch a wrong URL pattern that scans the wrong host, a storage change that drops a stored API key, or a classification drift where the extension and the app disagree about what a given URL is. Because the extension holds a user's API key, an api.ts regression that sends it to the wrong origin would also ship green.
recommendation: Add vitest (or node:test, matching the CLI's pattern) to extension/package.json with a "test" script, and add an extension test step to the CI extension job so it gates merges the same way the app's does. Start with the pure modules where a test is cheap and the failure is expensive: url-patterns.ts, scan-target.ts, format.ts, categories.ts, plans.ts. Then add a shared fixture list of URLs asserted identically against lib/scanner/scan-target-classify.ts in the app and the extension's own copy, so the two builds cannot drift apart unnoticed.

title: lib/scanner/protocol-findings.ts is at 0% while the banner parser it consumes is at 85%, so the entire ssh/smtp/imap/pop3/mongodb scan branch can report clean with no test failing
description: lib/scanner/protocol-findings.ts measures 0% statements / 0% branches / 0% functions (25 statements, 265 lines) and there is no tests/lib/scanner/protocol-findings.test.ts. Its header states it holds the 'Vulnerability builders for the non-HTTP protocol scan branch in execute-scan.ts (a URL whose scheme is ssh://, smtp://, imap://, pop3://, or mongodb://)' and that 'Finding IDs are derived deterministically from a checkId prefix + URL (see generateId), so the prefixes here MUST stay stable: changing one changes the ID of an existing finding type and breaks diffing between a user's older and newer scans of the same target'. The parsing layer beneath it is covered: lib/scanner/protocols/banner.ts is at 85.52%, with dedicated suites at tests/lib/scanner/protocols/banner-analysis, banner-tls-and-capability, and mongo-probe. So the suite proves the banner is parsed correctly and proves nothing about whether a finding is produced from it. For contrast, the three other low-coverage files under lib/scanner/checks/ (email.ts 3.03%, active-probes.ts 16.66%, reputation.ts 25%) are deliberate placeholders whose detectors return null, and are correctly not a gap.
impact: Two silent failures. A regression that drops a finding builder makes a protocol scan of a genuinely vulnerable host report clean, and the user has no signal that anything is wrong because the scan completes normally. A regression that changes an idPrefix silently breaks the scan-to-scan diff the file's own comment warns about, so the history view shows a resolved finding plus a new finding instead of one persistent one, in a product whose value proposition is tracking a host over time.
recommendation: Add tests/lib/scanner/protocol-findings.test.ts feeding a fixture BannerResult and MongoAuthProbeResult for each protocol and asserting: the expected finding is produced for a vulnerable banner and none for a clean one, and the finding id for a fixed (checkId, url) pair matches a hard-coded expected string. Pinning the ids in the assertion is what makes the prefix stability the header demands actually enforceable.

title: No test in the repo executes real SQL: 192 of 356 test files mock the pg pool and there is no test database, so column typos, broken CTEs, missing row locks, and schema drift are all invisible
description: Scope: the whole suite plus vitest.config.ts and the schema. 192 of the 356 test files contain `vi.mock("@/lib/database/db")`, and 195 reference a fake pool shape. Nothing in the repo starts a Postgres: no docker-compose service for tests, no testcontainers dependency, and the only tests that read DATABASE_URL do so to assert configuration behaviour, not to connect. Even tests/lib/database/db.test.ts, which cannot mock the module it tests, mocks one level lower at pg's Pool class with a FakePool. The result is that every SQL string in lib/ and app/ is treated as an opaque token: a mocked client returns whatever the test scripted regardless of what the query says, so a wrong column name, a dropped WHERE clause, a `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` that lost its lock, or a CTE that no longer returns its RETURNING row all pass. instrumentation.ts, the canonical schema at 3,639 lines with 72 CREATE TABLE and 97 CREATE INDEX statements, is explicitly excluded from coverage (vitest.config.ts:38) and only two test files reference it at all. There is also a documented contradiction: CLAUDE.md lists 'Mocking the database in tests' under What to avoid, while tests/README.md instructs 'Mock at the network and database boundary, not below it', and the suite follows the README.
impact: This is the structural reason a whole class of AUDIT-012 findings existed. Credit-ledger atomicity, the nine missing indexes in AUDIT-012#perf-15 that force full scans inside the cleanup transaction, and the function-wrapped columns in AUDIT-012#perf-16 that defeat an index are all properties of SQL text that the suite by construction cannot evaluate. The failure mode in production is a query that throws at runtime on a column that no longer exists, or an aggregate that returns silently wrong numbers, after a green CI run and a green deploy.
recommendation: Do not rewrite 192 files. Add one narrow integration suite gated on an env var, tests/integration/, that spins Postgres in the CI test job as a services: container, runs instrumentation.ts to build the schema, and exercises only the queries where correctness cannot be asserted any other way: the credit ledger reversals, reserveConcurrentScanSlot, incrementDailyCountCapped, and lib/database/cleanup.ts. Then resolve the doc contradiction by amending CLAUDE.md to match what the project actually does, so the next contributor is not choosing between two rules.

title: Twenty-seven of the seventy-one runtime dependencies have zero imports anywhere in the app, dragging 78 transitive packages and 77.6 MB into the production dependency graph
description: AUDIT-012#fe-13 found two of these (jspdf, jspdf-autotable). Extending that grep to all 86 declared packages, ripgrep for any quoted specifier (static import, `require(`, dynamic `import(`, type-only import) across app/, lib/, components/, tests/, scripts/, middleware.ts and every config file, with node_modules/.next/coverage/marketing/extension/cli/audits excluded, returns package.json itself as the only hit for twenty-five entries. Three groups, each with a different history.
