Per iteration: `checkAndRecordRequest` (line 637) costs `getDailyLimit` -> `getUserPlan` plus an UPSERT and possibly a re-read (lib/rate-limiting/daily-limits.ts:309/330/361/378) = 2-3 queries; `checkApiKeyRateLimit` (line 668) runs `pool.connect` + BEGIN + `SELECT id FROM api_keys WHERE id = $1 FOR UPDATE` (lib/api/api-keys.ts:489) + a 24h `COUNT(*)` over api_usage (line 505) + an INSERT (line 514) + COMMIT + an `UPDATE api_keys SET last_used_at` (line 528) + a `SELECT used_at ... LIMIT 1` (line 543) = 7 round trips holding a row lock; `runSingleScan` (line 688) adds `checkAccessRules` (2 queries) and an `INSERT INTO scan_history`. `MAX_URLS_BULK` defaults to 100 (lib/config/config-values.ts:543).
impact: A 100-URL bulk request performs on the order of 900-1000 serialized database round trips inside one HTTP handler, acquiring and releasing a `FOR UPDATE` lock on the same api_keys row 100 times, while holding pool connections throughout. Even at 2ms RTT that is two seconds of pure database latency layered on top of 100 sequential network scans.
recommendation: Hoist the per-user work out of the loop in app/api/v3/scan/bulk/route.ts:622: resolve the plan and daily limit once, charge quota for the whole batch in one capped statement, and record API usage once per batch (or as a single multi-row INSERT at the end) rather than per URL. Cache the access-rules result per host for the duration of the request.

title: Four routes select the full findings JSONB for an unbounded row set, including a GDPR export that buffers the entire admin audit log into memory twice
description: (a) app/api/v3/shares/route.ts:15-30 selects `summary, findings` for every share a user owns with no LIMIT, then JSON.parses each blob in JS at lines 32-36 -- and the only derived value is `findingsCount: findings.length` (line 50), which the `findings_count` column already stores. (b) app/api/v3/admin/audit-log/export/route.ts:79-88 runs `SELECT ... FROM admin_audit_log al LEFT JOIN users au ... LEFT JOIN users tu ... ORDER BY al.created_at DESC` with no WHERE and no LIMIT, buffers all rows into a JS array (line 81) and then `JSON.stringify(result.rows, null, 2)` (line 104) -- the entire audit table held in the Node heap twice. (c) lib/notifications/posture-digest.ts:80-93 runs `SELECT DISTINCT ON (url) url, findings FROM scan_history WHERE user_id = $1 AND status = 'completed' ORDER BY url, scanned_at DESC` with no LIMIT and no time bound, and it is called twice per user at lines 113-117. (d) app/api/v3/data-request/route.ts:167-174 selects `findings` for every scan the user ever ran.
impact: (b) is the sharpest: an admin clicking Export on a mature instance OOM-kills the single Node process that also runs every in-flight scan, since `admin_audit_log` grows on every staff action and there is no bound at all. (a) and (d) ship tens of megabytes per request for users with many scans. (c) makes the digest worker's cost scale with total history rather than with what the digest actually reports.
recommendation: Add `findings_count` to (a) and drop `findings` from the projection entirely. Stream (b) with a keyset-paged cursor and write CSV/NDJSON incrementally instead of building one string, and bound it with the same retention window lib/database/audit-log-archive.ts:80 uses. Give (c) a `LIMIT` and a `scanned_at > NOW() - INTERVAL '...'` bound, and project only the finding fields the digest renders. Page (d) or stream it to a file.

title: The nightly cleanup runs about thirty DELETEs, four of them full table scans, inside one 350-line transaction holding a pooled connection
description: `lib/database/cleanup.ts` opens `BEGIN` at line 114 and does not `COMMIT` until line 464, wrapping roughly thirty DELETE statements across sessions, rate_limits, tokens, scan_history, scan_finding_feedback, user_notifications, github_review_usage, ai_conversations and more in a single transaction on one pooled client. Four of those DELETEs cannot use an index and seq-scan their table (see perf-15): rate_limits (line 211), scan_finding_feedback (line 380), user_notifications (line 389), github_review_usage (line 401). None of the work is transactionally coupled -- these are independent retention prunes on unrelated tables.
impact: One of the 10 pool connections is held for the entire pass, and every row deleted stays locked for its duration, so any concurrent write touching those rows blocks. The four full scans make the pass length grow with total table size rather than with the number of rows actually being deleted. A failure at line 480 rolls back thirty prunes that had nothing to do with each other.
recommendation: Split the pass in lib/database/cleanup.ts:114-464 into one autocommitted statement per table (or small groups), with the batching pattern `DELETE ... WHERE ctid IN (SELECT ctid ... LIMIT 5000)` in a loop for the large tables, so no single statement holds locks for long. Add the four missing indexes from perf-15 first.

title: HTTPS targets are validated by DNS lookup and then re-resolved by undici at connect time, leaving the DNS-rebinding window the guard exists to close
description: validateScanTarget (lib/scanner/safe-fetch.ts:430-494) calls `lookup(hostname, {all:true})` and rejects the target if any returned address is private, then hands back `resolvedIp = addresses[0].address`. safeFetch pins that IP into the request URL only when the scheme is NOT https/wss (lib/scanner/safe-fetch.ts:601-620). For HTTPS, the `else if (isSecureProtocol && safety.resolvedIp)` branch at lib/scanner/safe-fetch.ts:621-624 does nothing but set a Host header; the URL keeps the hostname, so undici calls `dns.lookup` again at connect time. Node has no process-level DNS cache, so an attacker serving a TTL-0 A record from their own authoritative nameserver returns a public IP to validateScanTarget's query and 127.0.0.1 / 169.254.169.254 / an RFC1918 address to undici's query. This is deterministic, not a race. The same limitation is repeated verbatim in applyPinnedTarget (lib/scanner/async-checks.ts:2747-2759, `if (parsed.protocol !== "http:") return {url, init}`) and in pinToResolvedIp (lib/scanner/safe-fetch.ts:285), so every HTTPS probe in the scanner shares it. Both places document it as accepted ("for HTTPS the protection is the DNS re-resolution happening immediately before the request"), which is not a protection at all. Note that the TLS-specific checks got this right: lib/scanner/checks/tls.ts:261-267 and lib/scanner/async-checks.ts:2268-2278 both `tls.connect({host: safeIp, servername: hostname})`, pinning the IP while keeping SNI, which is exactly the pattern the fetch layer is missing.
impact: An attacker who controls a nameserver can make every HTTPS request the scanner issues land on an internal address of their choosing. Certificate validation stops them reading a response body (the cert will not match their hostname), but the TCP connect and TLS ClientHello still happen, and the difference between an immediate RST, a TLS alert, and a full timeout is a working blind port/service scanner for the network VulnRadar runs in, driven from an unauthenticated /api/v3/demo-scan request. It also means the entire private-IP block list is advisory on the HTTPS path, so any future change that relaxes cert checking (the scanner already uses rejectUnauthorized:false elsewhere) turns this into a full read primitive.
recommendation: Pin the connect address without breaking SNI. In lib/scanner/safe-fetch.ts, build a per-request undici `Agent` whose `connect.lookup` returns the already-validated `safety.resolvedIp` (`new Agent({ connect: { lookup: (host, opts, cb) => cb(null, [{address: resolvedIp, family: isIP(resolvedIp)}]) } })`) and pass it as `dispatcher` in the fetch init, for https and http alike. That preserves the hostname for SNI and certificate validation while guaranteeing the socket goes to the address that was checked. Then delete the http-only branch at :601-624, apply the same dispatcher in applyPinnedTarget (lib/scanner/async-checks.ts:2747) and pinToResolvedIp (lib/scanner/safe-fetch.ts:273), and drop the "HTTPS relies on the immediate re-resolution" comments they all copy.

title: The ToS gate blocks the unsubscribe link in every marketing email
description: components/auth/tos-gate.tsx:9 sets SKIP_TOS_PATHS to ["/login", "/signup", "/legal"]. The logged-out path is fine because :28-31 sets status skip when /api/v3/auth/me is not ok. The exposure is a signed-in user with pending or needs_reaccept status, for whom the page renders at opacity-20 blur-xs pointer-events-none behind TosModal (:77-91). /unsubscribe, /verify-email and /reset-password are not in the skip list.
impact: The unsubscribe link in every marketing email is gated behind accepting updated terms. Coupled with auth-05, the unsubscribe flow is compromised at both ends.
recommendation: Add "/unsubscribe", "/verify-email", "/reset-password" and "/forgot-password" to SKIP_TOS_PATHS.

title: Auth pages prerender a null Suspense fallback, so first paint is empty and the indexable /login is one empty div
description: app/reset-password/page.tsx:41 uses Suspense fallback={null}, prerendered into the static HTML, while the pitch column is hidden lg:block. First paint on a phone is wordmark, empty band, footer. The same shape at app/login/page.tsx:12 and app/signup/page.tsx:12 replaces the entire page.
impact: A blank first paint on the three highest-intent pages in the product, and the HTML a crawler receives for the indexable /login is a single empty div.
recommendation: Give each Suspense a real skeleton fallback.

title: The unsubscribe page prints an email address with no break-all and scrolls the page sideways
description: app/unsubscribe/page.tsx:293 and :324 render redactEmail() output with no break-all, while three sibling components have it.
impact: A long address scrolls the whole page horizontally.
recommendation: Add break-all.

title: The unsubscribe page crushes 19 preference rows into max-w-sm while an unused wide variant exists for exactly this screen
description: app/unsubscribe/page.tsx:393 renders a 19-row preference list inside max-w-sm, leaving about 1050px empty on either side at 1440px. components/auth/auth-layout.tsx:9-11 documents an unused width="wide" prop with a docstring saying it is 'for the one screen that is a list rather than a form', which is this screen.
impact: The page is needlessly cramped, and the fix already exists in the codebase unused.
recommendation: Pass width="wide".

title: The browser session viewer renders raw runtime error strings to the user
description: app/browser/[id]/page.tsx:153-155 sets `e instanceof Error ? e.message : ...` and renders it at :546. A stale-deploy HTML response therefore surfaces `Unexpected token '<', "<!DOCTYPE "... is not valid JSON` to the user. The same shape at :319-323 renders {logsError} raw at :670-672, which can be literally 'HTTP 502'. For contrast components/scanner/dashboard-error-state.tsx:257-275 deliberately shows the scanner's message, and that is safe because app/api/v3/scan/route.ts:288-292 sets details to a fixed string.
impact: Users see JSON parser internals. Given the known stale-deploy chunk-404 failure mode in this project, this is the error they are most likely to hit.
recommendation: Keep the raw text in console.error and render a fixed sentence.

title: The subscription is created before card validation, leaving an orphan incomplete subscription on every typo
description: components/billing/stripe-checkout.tsx:210 creates the Stripe subscription before calling elements.submit(). The other three billing components validate first and carry a comment explaining why.
impact: Every mistyped card leaves an orphan incomplete subscription on the customer record, polluting billing data and potentially triggering dunning.
recommendation: Call elements.submit() first, matching components/billing/ai-credit-checkout.tsx.

title: The checkout success page only understands subscriptions, so credit top-ups warn about a payment that succeeded
description: app/checkout/success/checkout-success-content.tsx:13 is the return_url for all four checkout flows but only polls verify-subscription. A redirect-method credit top-up polls for about 22.5 seconds and then warns the payment could not be confirmed. redirect_status=failed is ignored entirely, so a genuinely failed payment also lands on a page implying success is pending.
impact: A successful purchase is reported as possibly failed, and a failed purchase is reported as probably fine. Both directions are wrong on the money path.
recommendation: Branch on the product type in the return URL and read redirect_status.

title: The support tickets section renders nothing while loading, so /contact looks like the feature is missing
description: components/contact/support-tickets.tsx:174 is `if (isLoading) return null`, under the first and most prominent category on /contact.
impact: On a cold load the page appears not to have a ticket feature at all.
recommendation: Render a skeleton instead of null.

title: /donate removes its own fallback link at the moment it is needed and traps the back button in a redirect loop
description: app/donate/page.tsx:14-22 redirects via window.location.href after 100ms and sets redirected true. At :51-60 the manual 'Continue to Stripe' button renders only when !redirected, and a thank-you message replaces it when redirected. Three defects compound: the fallback disappears exactly when the automatic redirect has failed; location.href rather than location.replace() leaves /donate in history, so Back from Stripe returns here and re-fires after 100ms; and the page has no nav, no <main> and no footer, so a stranded user has no way off it.
impact: A user whose redirect fails is shown a thank-you for a donation that never happened, with no link to complete it and no navigation. Pressing Back from Stripe creates an inescapable loop.
recommendation: Use location.replace(), keep the fallback link rendered unconditionally, drop the premature thank-you, and wrap the page in PublicPageShell.

title: Checkout columns are misaligned between 768px and 1024px by a hardcoded top padding
description: app/checkout/[productId]/page.tsx:306 uses a magic md:pt-[120px] to align the second column.
impact: The two columns visibly misalign across the whole tablet band on the payment page.
recommendation: Align with a grid row rather than a hardcoded pixel offset.

title: /checks ships roughly 754 list items and 190KB of HTML that never paints
description: app/checks/page.tsx:147-188 renders an <li> for every one of roughly 754 checks across 18 categories, each with a SeverityPill carrying three inline style properties and a Link, all inside collapsed <details> elements.
impact: Slow first paint on a phone, on the page whose entire purpose is to rank in search and be read by mobile arrivals.
recommendation: Inline only the first N categories and link the rest to the existing /checks/category/[category] pages, or move the full index behind a crawlable ?all=1. The 754 individual check pages are intentional SEO surface and stay.

title: The root 404 has no public chrome and its primary button sends logged-out visitors to the dashboard
description: No in-scope content route has its own not-found.tsx, so all three dynamic content routes fall through to the root one, which renders no LandingNav, no Footer, and a primary button linking to ROUTES.DASHBOARD. The same shape applies to app/error.tsx:103.
impact: A logged-out visitor landing on a stale /checks/some-renamed-id from a search result gets a chrome-less 404 whose main button bounces them through middleware to /login. The likeliest visitor to a dead check URL is exactly the person with no account.
recommendation: Add app/checks/not-found.tsx and app/alternatives/not-found.tsx wrapping SeoPageShell, or make the root 404's primary button conditional on auth and default it to ROUTES.LANDING.

title: Twelve schema columns are written and never read, or defined and never written
description: Verified dead, each with the grep that found no live reference: users.beta_access (:303) hardcoded false in every INSERT (lib/auth/auth.ts:282,361,382; staff-invite/[token]/route.ts:199), no UPDATE, no gate; users.email_session_revoked (:317) a legacy duplicate whose nine live references all resolve to notification_preferences; users.daily_scan_limit (:304) see drift-05; broadcast_recipients.opened_at and .clicked_at (:1155-1156) DDL only; broadcast_messages.scheduled_at (:1137) inserted but no worker consumes it and status is hardcoded 'draft' then 'sent', so the CHECK values 'scheduled' and 'cancelled' are unwritable; broadcast_messages.message_type (:1135) hardcoded "email" by the UI and never read by the send path (:504); data_requests.completed_at (:876) DDL only, the route uses downloaded_at; system_settings.setting_type (:1121) DDL only; gifted_subscriptions.reason (:950) selected in the GDPR export but the only INSERT (admin/route.ts:1671) omits it and the gift dialog has no field; badges.is_limited (:496) only ever inserted as false with no UPDATE anywhere; api_keys.team_id (:931) no reference in lib/api/api-keys.ts or app/api/v3/keys; scan_screenshots.width and .height (:1381-1382) written at lib/scanner/page-screenshot.ts:295, never selected, consumers read the result_meta copy.
impact: Schema noise that misleads anyone reading the model, plus three cases (beta_access, message_type, scheduled_at) that look like shipped features and are not.
recommendation: Decide per column: wire it or drop it. Deletions need owner sign-off. beta_access, broadcast scheduling and broadcast message_type are the three worth a product decision rather than a silent drop.

title: Fifteen permission constants gate nothing, including two for a reports feature that does not exist
description: Dead constants in lib/auth/permissions-client.ts: VIEW_USER_API_KEYS (:29), DELETE_ANY_TEAM (:76), VIEW_REPORTS (:80) and RESOLVE_REPORTS (:81) - there is no reports feature or table at all - VIEW_DEBUG_INFO (:92), CLEAR_CACHE (:94), SEND_USER_EMAILS (:85), ACCESS_ADMIN_PANEL (:11), ACCESS_STAFF_PAGE (:12) granted to six roles while app/staff does not exist, VIEW_USER_SESSIONS (:27), VIEW_BADGES (:34), VIEW_ALL_SCANS (:41), VIEW_SCAN_STATS (:43), VIEW_SUBSCRIPTIONS (:47), MANAGE_SUBSCRIPTIONS (:48). requireModerator() at lib/auth/authorization.ts:102-122 has zero call sites. Separately, several cards render ungated where a permission exists for them: the API Keys card at user-detail-panel.tsx:2561, sessions at :2667, all-scans at :2507, and badges at admin/route.ts:281-286 which has no permission call unlike its neighbours at :249 and :294.
impact: An operator granting or withholding these permissions changes nothing, which is a security-adjacent false assurance. The ungated cards are the mirror image: data visible to staff roles that were never granted access to it.
recommendation: Split into two passes: wire the four ungated cards to their existing permissions first, since that is a real access-control gap; then delete or implement the fifteen dead constants.

title: Nineteen API capabilities exist with no UI control, each with a specific screen it belongs on
description: Verified by reading each handler. POST /api/v3/scan/import-spec (parses OpenAPI 3, Swagger 2 and Postman, returns targets) has no UI caller; API.SCAN_IMPORT_SPEC exists at lib/config/client-constants.ts:145 referenced only by the changelog - belongs on the bulk tab of components/scanner/scan-form.tsx. Authenticated crawl is unreachable: app/api/v3/scan/crawl/route.ts:216,300-337 accepts the same auth block, but app/dashboard/page.tsx:415-449 routes any request carrying auth to the single-page endpoint, so deep plus a login silently downgrades. PATCH /api/v3/teams/members (role change, with ceiling and self-demotion guards) has no caller; the only way to change a teammate's role is remove and re-invite - belongs on components/teams/team-members-list.tsx:160. PATCH /api/v3/account/discord (syncAvatar, syncName) unreachable while components/modals/discord-profile-modal.tsx:27-28 has exactly those checkboxes but POSTs OAuth query-string values to /api/v3/auth/update, so it only works in the seconds after connecting. Badge revoke (DELETE /api/v3/badge/site?scanId=N, sets revoked_at) has no caller, so a badge pasted into a public README cannot be killed - belongs under the ScopeToggle at components/badge/badge-preview.tsx:261. Support tickets cannot be reopened: the route permits it at app/api/v3/support-tickets/[id]/route.ts:321-328 but both UIs only send resolved and closed, and replying to a closed ticket 409s. The updater can only install the newest release (app/api/v3/admin/updater/apply/route.ts:94,120-123 accepts any targetVersion; components/admin/features/updater-manager.tsx:185 always sends status.latest) so there is no rollback or pin. /api/v3/health returns schema_version vs schema_required, missing_tables, latency and pool stats and has no consumer, so a self-hoster needing a migration has no in-app signal. Stripe setup is curl-only, and both routes gate on role !== ADMIN exactly (setup-products/route.ts:31, setup-webhook/route.ts:36) which locks out super_admin unlike every other admin route. Also: teamId on schedules and webhooks, webhook type pinning (both UI paths hardcode "auto"), GitHub repo scan branch/ref, per-finding feedback notes, browser session viewport and ttlSeconds (the latter hardcoded to 360 at scan-actions-menu.tsx:384, defeating the admin setting), security alerts limit/offset/severity/user_id (hardcoded to 100 so alert 101 is unreachable), admin AI-conversations userId filter, admin notification email tone (hardcoded "info"), history rescan dropping all original scan options, scan source 'scheduled' rendering as "Web", admin content and public directory page sizes, and markAllRead on the notification bell.
impact: Nineteen shipped backend capabilities that no user can reach. Several are not conveniences: badge revoke has no alternative, authenticated crawl silently does something other than what was asked, and the health endpoint is the only signal a self-hoster has that their schema is behind.
recommendation: Triage by user harm rather than effort. Highest first: authenticated crawl (silent wrong behaviour), badge revoke (no alternative exists), team member role change (workaround is destructive), support ticket reopen (dead end), health panel (self-host blocker). The rest are ordinary missing controls.

title: Four backend capabilities are gated behind conditions nothing can satisfy
description: domains.team_id (instrumentation.ts:3176) is read for team access at app/api/v3/domains/route.ts:33, but the INSERT at :120 omits it, no PATCH exists anywhere under app/api/v3/domains/ (exports are GET, POST, DELETE plus verify POST), all four UPDATE/INSERT statements skip it, and components/profile/tabs/domains-section.tsx:147 hardcodes team_id: null - yet app/docs/teams/page.tsx:425 documents it as a feature. DEFAULT_API_KEY_DAILY_LIMIT (registry.ts:1527-1536) is admin-editable and read at lib/api/api-keys.ts:70 via `dailyLimit ?? await getSetting(...)`, but generateApiKey has exactly one production caller (app/api/v3/keys/route.ts:95) which always passes an explicit number, so the branch is dead; compounding, app/docs/api/page.tsx:738 and app/docs/rate-limits/page.tsx:173 tell users the default is 50 while the real value is the plan's apiRequestsPerDay, 25 on Free. access_rules.is_active = false is writable via the API but the list query filters WHERE is_active = true (admin/features/route.ts:168), so a deactivated rule vanishes and can never be reactivated. The empty-string state of CHROME_WEB_STORE_URL and FIREFOX_ADDON_URL (registry.ts:397-412) is documented as falling back to a packaged release, but the admin write goes through z.url() which rejects "", the env path skips empty overrides (runtime-config.ts:89), and reset restores a non-empty default - and the fallback UI does not exist either, since app/docs/extension/page.tsx:113,139 link unconditionally under a hardcoded 'Live' badge.
impact: Four documented behaviours that cannot occur. The API key limit case additionally publishes a wrong number to users in two docs pages.
recommendation: Correct the two docs pages about the API key default immediately, since that is user-facing misinformation. Then either implement domains.team_id (a PATCH route plus a selector) or remove it and its docs claim.

title: Two entitlements are enforced but never advertised, and one has no admin setting at all
description: The crawl page-selection limit is hardcoded at lib/billing/crawl-page-limits.ts:18-23 (25/50/100/250) and enforced at app/api/v3/scan/crawl/route.ts:258, but a grep for CRAWL_PAGES in lib/config/registry.ts returns zero. It is the only per-plan entitlement with no registry key, so it is absent from Admin > Settings > Billing and from components/pricing/pricing-features.tsx, surfacing only at point of use (components/scanner/crawl-url-selector.tsx:50). githubReviewTokensPerWindow is enforced per plan but no plan's features array mentions GitHub review (only AI review tokens at lib/billing/catalog.ts:141,174,205), so a Free user hits a hard 403 with no prior signal. Separately, lib/billing/github-review-usage.ts:365-372 implements a free-plan trial whose own comment reads 'Hidden trial, never advertised on the pricing page', while Free's githubReviewTokensPerWindow of 0 makes components/pricing/pricing-features.tsx:85-89 render a cross for Free.
impact: Two invisible paywalls that users meet as a 403 rather than as a plan comparison, and a genuine free-tier benefit that the pricing page actively denies exists.
recommendation: Add BILLING_*_CRAWL_PAGES registry keys and a Scanning row on /pricing. Add a GitHub review row to the plan comparison. Decide whether the hidden trial should be advertised; if it stays hidden, stop rendering a cross for a capability Free actually has.

title: The public scans table uses fixed pixel columns that crush the hostname at tablet widths
description: components/public-scans/public-scans-table.tsx:7 and components/public-scans/public-scan-row.tsx:22 use grid-cols-[1fr_150px_150px_90px] with gap-4, which is 390px of fixed columns plus 48px of gaps. At the sm breakpoint (640px) the Site column collapses to about 120px so nearly every hostname truncates, while 'Verdict' renders the word 'Clean' inside 150px.
impact: The one column carrying the information is starved while two columns hold whitespace, on a public directory page.
recommendation: Use sm:grid-cols-[minmax(0,1fr)_90px_150px_120px], or move the grid to the md breakpoint and keep the stacked layout through tablet.

title: A blurred full-screen AI modal opens the instant results land, so a finished scan reads as still working
description: app/dashboard/page.tsx:690-692 opens AiChoiceModal on completion, a fixed inset-0 backdrop-blur-xs overlay (components/scanner/ai-choice-modal.tsx:36). Results render underneath but the user must click Skip to see them.
impact: Perceived latency on top of real latency. The scan finishes and the user is shown a blur, which is indistinguishable from more waiting.
recommendation: Do not auto-open on completion. Offer the AI summary as an action on the results view instead, so the payoff of the scan is the first thing visible.

title: Five different page shells across the public surface, with /pricing hand-rolled and /donate having none
description: PublicPageShell (components/shared/public-page-shell.tsx:32) swaps `isLoggedIn ? <Header/> : <LandingNav/>` at :58, covering /changelog, /compare, /contact, /security, /host/[hostname], /public-scans, /shared/[token]. DocsShell, LegalShell and SeoPageShell all use LandingNav unconditionally. /pricing is hand-rolled and renders <LandingNav /> twice (app/pricing/page.tsx:71 and :150) despite computing isLoggedIn at :66. /donate has no nav, no <main> and no footer at all. LandingNav is itself auth-aware (components/landing/landing-nav.tsx:104), so the swap is redundant.
impact: A signed-in user clicking Changelog, then Docs, then Changelog watches the header change identity twice. /donate is a page with no way off it.
recommendation: Move /pricing and /donate onto PublicPageShell and pick one convention for the signed-in header across the four public shells. The non-negotiable half is shell-01: the skip-link id should live in one shell rather than being forgotten by three.

title: Any non-OK teams response logs a signed-in user out
description: app/teams/page.tsx:109-113 is `if (!res.ok) { router.push("/login"); return; }` with no status check. Every sibling gates on 401 and 403 specifically (app/history/page.tsx:226, app/assets/page.tsx:74). The same shape exists at app/profile/page.tsx:296.
impact: A transient 500, 503 or 429 bounces a still-authenticated user to the login screen, which reads as a session bug and erodes trust in the auth system.
recommendation: Gate the redirect on 401 and 403 and render an error state otherwise, matching the sibling pages.

title: No push/proactive alerting on production incidents -- everything is pull-based
description: There is no external error-tracking or alerting SDK wired into the app (no Sentry/Datadog/etc. in package.json). The admin System > Error Logs panel (a genuinely good feature -- see the 'checked and fine' note) captures console.error calls into a searchable table, and /api/v3/health returns 503 on a dead DB, but both are pull: an operator only learns something is wrong by opening /admin or by having set up their own external uptime monitor against /api/v3/health, neither of which this repo configures. A dead scheduled-scans worker, a run of failed Stripe webhooks, or a DB outage at 3am produces rows in a table and a 503 response that nobody is watching until a customer complains. Evidence: package.json has no @sentry/*, datadog, or similar dependency; app/api/v3/admin/error-logs/route.ts is a GET/DELETE the admin has to visit -- nothing pushes its contents anywhere.
recommendation: NOT YET APPLIED -- reported for review. Recommendation: Wire the health endpoint into an external uptime monitor (even a free one) that pages someone on 503, and/or add a lightweight Sentry-style SDK for exception capture with alerting, since the in-app error log viewer is a good diagnostic tool but not an alerting system.

title: s3-bucket-exposed: s3-bucket-exposed (medium severity) fires on any S3-hosted public asset URL, which is normal, intentional CDN usage
description: The check is a bare regex match for any `https://*.s3.amazonaws.com` URL with zero filtering — presence alone is treated as an "exposure". Public S3 buckets used to serve static assets (images, downloads, PDFs) are a deliberate, extremely common hosting pattern, not a misconfiguration. Verified: `` matches. Trigger: Any website that hosts a logo, product image, or downloadable file on a public S3 bucket (widespread practice — S3 static asset hosting is a standard, documented AWS use case), e.g. ``.
recommendation: Either drop this to "info" severity (bare presence of an S3 URL is not itself a risk signal), or require corroborating signal before flagging at "medium": only fire when the referenced object path itself suggests sensitive content (matches /backup|\.env|config|private|dump|\.sql|credentials/i), analogous to how other checks in this group require adjacent risk context instead of firing on bare presence.

title: cache-control-no-store-missing: Sensitive-path detection uses raw substring matches that hit unrelated public routes
description: Both cache-control-no-store-missing (lines 962-977) and cache-control-missing (lines 100-120) use the identical `.includes()` substring list `[/login,/signin,/signup,/register,/admin,/api/auth,/session,/account]`. Because these are plain substring checks rather than path-segment matches, `/api/auth` matches any path merely containing that substring (e.g. `/api/authors`), `/session` matches `/sessions`, and `/account` matches `/accounting` -- none of which are actually authentication/session endpoints. Trigger: A blog/CMS REST endpoint `/api/authors/42` (common on Ghost, WordPress-style, or custom Next.js content APIs) or an events site's public schedule page `/sessions/keynote-address`, or a fintech marketing page `/accounting/reports` -- all public, non-sensitive routes that get flagged as 'sensitive page path detected' for lacking Cache-Control: no-store.
recommendation: Replace the `.includes()` calls in both detectors with path-segment-aware matching, e.g. `/(^|\/)(login|signin|signup|register|admin|session|account)(\/|$)/i.test(path)` plus a separate `/(^|\/)api\/auth(\/|$)/i.test(path)` for the auth-API case, so `/api/authors`, `/sessions`, and `/accounting` no longer match.

title: mixed-protocol-content: Counts plain <a href="http://..."> navigation links as mixed content, a bug this codebase already documented and fixed for the sibling headers.ts check but not here
description:
detectMixedContent (lines 29-45) matches `(?:src|href|action)\s*=\s*["']http://` against every tag in the body, which includes ordinary navigation links and
(already covered separately by form-action-http). A plain hyperlink is never fetched as a subresource by the browser and triggers no mixed-content warning or block. headers.ts's own `mixed-content` detector explicitly documents fixing this exact false positive ('A plain is regular navigation, never fetched as a subresource -- it must not count here'), but that scoping was never applied to this separate ssl.ts implementation of the same underlying concept. Trigger: Any HTTPS page containing an ordinary outbound citation/reference link to an HTTP-only external resource, e.g. a blog post or documentation page linking `source` -- gets counted as an N-count 'mixed-content reference' even though nothing is fetched insecurely.
recommendation: Scope the pattern to actual subresource-loading tags only (script/img/iframe/video/audio/source/object/embed src=, and <link rel=stylesheet href=), mirroring headers.ts's `mixed-content` detector, and drop bare href on <a> and action on <form> (form action is already covered by form-action-http).

title: idor-sequential-id-in-url: Fires on Drupal's default /user/{uid} entity route, a standard CMS path used across a large share of the web
description: The regex `/\/(?:api\/)?(?:v\d+\/)?(?:user|account|invoice|order|profile)s?\/([1-9]\d{0,4})(?:\/|$|\?)/i` matches any URL path shaped like `/user/<n>` or `/profile/<n>` with no API/version prefix required. Drupal (a major CMS, powering a large share of government, university, and enterprise sites) uses exactly this path -- `/user/{uid}` -- as its default, framework-generated user-profile route, and by Drupal convention uid 1 is the site's first/admin account, so `/user/1` is an extremely common, often intentionally reachable URL across the Drupal ecosystem (frequently linked exactly this way, e.g. the pattern seen at drupal.org/user/1-style links). Scanning any Drupal site's default user page produces a 'Sequential Numeric ID in URL (IDOR Risk)' finding for what is simply the CMS's standard content-routing path, not an owner-scoped API resource. Trigger: Scanning any stock Drupal site at its default admin/user page, e.g. `https://<any-drupal-site>/user/1` -- confirmed the check's own regex matches this exact path (verified: `/\/(?:api\/)?(?:v\d+\/)?(?:user|account|invoice|order|profile)s?\/([1-9]\d{0,4})(?:\/|$|\?)/i.exec("https://example.edu/user/1")` returns a match with id=1).
recommendation: Require an `api/` or `v\d+/` prefix specifically for the `user` and `profile` nouns (the two that collide with common CMS content-routing conventions), while leaving `account`/`invoice`/`order` matchable bare since those remain reliably owner-scoped in normal usage. Concretely: split the alternation so `(?:api\/|v\d+\/)(?:user|profile)s?\/(\d+)` requires an API/version prefix, while `(?:api\/)?(?:v\d+\/)?(?:account|invoice|order)s?\/(\d+)` keeps the current bare-path matching.

title: POST /api/v3/scan/feedback accepts a caller-supplied scanHistoryId with no ownership check, letting any user attach fabricated feedback to (and trigger a forced recompute + host_reputation cascade against) any scan in the system
description:
FeedbackSchema only validates that `scanHistoryId` is a positive integer (app/api/v3/scan/feedback/route.ts:10); the POST handler never verifies `scan_history.user_id === session.userId` for it before inserting into scan_finding_feedback (scan_history_id FK just needs to reference an existing row, per instrumentation.ts's `scan_history_id INTEGER REFERENCES scan_history(id) ON DELETE SET NULL`) and before calling `recomputeScanScore(scanHistoryId)` (line 64). This breaks the exact convention the codebase documents for itself elsewhere -- e.g. app/api/v3/webhooks/[id]/route.ts's own comment: 'Every other per-resource route in this codebase ... verifies ownership in the same UPDATE ... WHERE id = $n AND user_id = $n statement ... so a [resource] ID belonging to another user can never be [mutated]' -- a pattern this route does not follow for scanHistoryId.

Impact: any authenticated user (including free tier) can POST arbitrary {findingId, findingUrl, verdict, notes} tied to any other user's scan_history_id (IDs are small sequential integers, trivially enumerable), polluting the scan_finding_feedback table that idx_scan_finding_feedback_finding_id (finding_id, verdict) indexes for the admin 'Engine Feedback' false-positive-rate aggregation (CONFIG_ENGINE_FEEDBACK_NOISE_THRESHOLD_PERCENT). It also forces recomputeScanScore to run an UPDATE against another user's scan_history row and against host_reputation `WHERE source_scan_id = scanHistoryId` for a scan the caller doesn't own and never touched otherwise -- a write side-effect triggered purely by an unauthenticated-for-that-resource request parameter. Evidence: app/api/v3/scan/feedback/route.ts:7-13 (FeedbackSchema, scanHistoryId has no ownership tie), line 39-54 (INSERT uses scanHistoryId as-is, no ownership SELECT), line 63-65 (`if (scanHistoryId) { recomputeScanScore(scanHistoryId).catch(() => {}); }`); lib/scanner/recompute-scan-score.ts:58-112 (reads/writes scan_history and host_reputation by that raw id).
recommendation: NOT YET APPLIED -- reported for review. Recommendation: Before inserting or calling recomputeScanScore, verify the caller owns the scan (or has team access, matching the pattern in app/api/v3/history/[id]/share/route.ts): `SELECT user_id FROM scan_history WHERE id = $1 AND user_id = $2`, returning 400/404 if scanHistoryId is present but not owned by session.userId. If it's intentional that feedback can reference a scan the user doesn't own (e.g. a shared/public scan they're reviewing), explicitly document that trust decision and still avoid triggering the host_reputation-cascading recompute for a scan outside the caller's own history.

title: CSRF exemption `pathname.startsWith("/api/v3/webhooks/")` intended only for the Stripe webhook receiver also exempts the user's own session-authenticated webhook-edit endpoint
description:
middleware.ts's isExemptFromCsrf() exempts any path starting with `/api/v3/webhooks/` from the Origin/Referer CSRF check, with the stated rationale 'Exempt endpoints authenticate the caller some other way (signed payload, server-issued secret, etc.)' -- true for app/api/v3/webhooks/stripe/route.ts (verified via STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET), but the prefix match also matches app/api/v3/webhooks/[id]/route.ts's PATCH handler, which edits a webhook's url/name/type/active flag using ONLY the session cookie for authentication (no signature, no secondary secret) -- exactly the class of endpoint the CSRF check exists to protect. This violates the function's own documented invariant: 'Keep this list narrow -- every entry needs a clear non-CSRF trust boundary,' which is not true for /api/v3/webhooks/[id].

Current practical exploitability is reduced (not eliminated) by the session cookie's `sameSite: 'lax'` attribute (lib/auth/auth.ts:65): a cross-site fetch/XHR PATCH (the only way to reach this endpoint, since HTML forms cannot send PATCH) does not carry SameSite=Lax cookies today in a standards-compliant browser, so this is currently a redundant-layer failure rather than an immediately exploitable one -- but it is a real gap in the app's primary, documented CSRF defense, and would become directly exploitable if a future route is added under this prefix that's reachable via GET/POST top-level navigation, or in any user-agent context where SameSite enforcement is weaker than assumed. Evidence: middleware.ts:314-327 (`pathname.startsWith("/api/v3/webhooks/")` in isExemptFromCsrf); app/api/v3/webhooks/[id]/route.ts:23-32 (PATCH authenticates via getSession() / cookie only, matches the exempted prefix); app/api/v3/webhooks/stripe/route.ts:38-40 (the actual signature-verified endpoint the exemption was written for).
recommendation: NOT YET APPLIED -- reported for review. Recommendation: Narrow the exemption to the exact Stripe path: `pathname === "/api/v3/webhooks/stripe"` instead of a prefix match, so /api/v3/webhooks/[id] (and any future path under this prefix) goes through the normal Origin/Referer CSRF check like every other session-authenticated mutating route.
